Convention Instructions
1) Come to the camp with open heart and teachable spirit, Bible, Jotter, Camp programme and pen.
2) We will be fasting throughout this year’s convention. It is therefore important to sincerely prepare your heart to
 seek the Lord and devote every available moment to prayer as we humble ourselves before Him and trust Him for
 a great visitation.
3) Please do not come to the tent of meeting (auditorium) with earpiece, phone chargers, Food/small
 chops/chewables and mobile phones/Tablets. For those who want to use mobile phones/tablet applications as
 Bible, we suggest you avoid distraction to yourself and others and come with hard copy Bible. It is a temptation
 when a call, SMS, chat, Facebook message, tweet, gaming alerts etc. comes in as you use the Bible part of the
 phone. Avoid anything that may create divided attention at a special convention like this. COME WITH HARD COPY
 BIBLES AND AVOID USE OF PHONES AS BIBLE
4) In the hostel, please do not come with expensive personal items like Laptop, I-pad etc. Stove, Pots, Boiling Ring,
 Adaptor, Electric Iron, Football, Electric Kettle and any form of sharp objects are disallowed and will be seized
 when found.
5) All campers must dress appropriately in ways that glorify God.
6) All sisters must cover their head/hair. All skimpy, body-revealing or tight-fitted dresses are strongly discouraged.
 All brothers must dress decently with no caps/hats at the tent of meeting.
7) We are using multiple hostels within the Redemption Camp and it is important that all campers move with
 everyone at the same time. We have also arranged for the law enforcement agencies to help with the movement.
 No one is allowed to move alone
8) No camper should bring merchandise of any kind for sale or broker a sales arrangement with an external trader.
 No camper is here for trading (e.g photography, selling of any kind)
9) All individual/group Christian books, magazines, fliers, programme, posters, cassettes and CDs/VCDs/DVDs for
 sale/exhibition/display or free distribution must be approved by the National Coordinator or his delegates.
10) While we have no convention this T-shirt this year, we remind all participants that we do not allow customised "T"
 shirt with individual names, we live to glorify the Lord, in words and in deed.
11) This Convention is not a pleasure trip; each day should be spent studying, fellowshipping, praying and planning to
 fulfill God's purpose for your life. Do not disappoint God.
12) Anointing flows best when the atmosphere is made conducive. Avoid foolish talking, abusive language, jesting,
 chatting, use of mobile phones and unnecessary distractions.
13) Be patient: One of the tactics of the devil to hinder your blessing is to cause you to be impatient with God and
 with your fellow brethren. Bear with whatever inconveniences you may encounter. Do not grumble.
14) Stay in with God: Nobody is permitted to leave the camp, except on written approval of the Camp Commandant
 through the Head, Registration Unit. Do not go outside for any purchases, the supermarket is there to attend to
 your needs.
15) Be clean: Cleanliness is next to Godliness. Keep yourself, the hostels and the camp clean. Do not litter or mess
 around. Dust bins have been provided for use. There are special water tanks provided for cleaning of hands. Make
 sure you wash your hands after you use any of the conveniences.]
16) Be available: Make sure you attend all sessions, jot your points and take time to pray.
17) Be healed: If you are not feeling fine, feel free to consult the First Aid Clinic or report to any Camp Worker.
18) Counselling: For career, emotional and spiritual counselling, visit the Counseling Department.
19) Wear your tag at all times and do not take another person's bed spaces. All tags/registration will have specific bed
 spaces – ONLY GO TO ROOMS/BED SPACES ALLOCATED TO YOU. If you did not register, don't attempt to go to any
 hostel that is not allocated to you. Do not follow your friends to their rooms, please check the room and bed space
 that is specifically allocated to you.
20) Be careful of new friends you exchange your contact details with at the camp. Please report any strange behavior,
 suggestive/immoral exchange of materials /videos/contents/messages/papers made by any camper to you or
 someone around you.
21) Great programmes do not make a great person, only great decisions do. As a true revival army, spend time
 reflecting on the messages and making decisions to live by after the Convention. For only the doers of the word
 shall be blessed!

 ~5~

22) The Convention is the beginning of a journey. The Convention will only be meaningful if you go back to your local
 fellowship and be an active agent of revival through active involvement as a revival army in your local Church,
 campus and community.

"For the Lord thy God walketh in the midst of the CAMP to deliver thee… therefore shall thy camp be HOLY that He sees
no unclean thing in thee" Deut. 23:14.

Health advisory from the Clinic Ministry
“Beloved, I pray that you may prosper in all things and be in health, just as your soul prospers.” 3 John 1:2 (NKJV)

We give all glory to Jehovah-Rapha, the Lord our Healer, for preserving us in sound health throughout our previous
conventions. We are confident that His healing presence will again abide with us throughout this year’s Bootcamp
Convention, in Jesus’ name. Amen.
As we prepare ourselves spiritually for this life-transforming convention, let us also prepare ourselves physically, because
our bodies are the temple of the Holy Spirit.

“Do you not know that your bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit...?” 1 Cor. 6:19

Kindly take note of the following health guidelines:

(1) Prepare yourself health-wise before coming
“A prudent person foresees danger and takes precautions.” Proverbs 22:3 (NLT)
 • Ensure that you get adequate rest in the days leading up to the convention.
 • Eat balanced meals and remain well hydrated.
 • If you develop any illness before the convention, seek appropriate medical attention promptly.
 • Avoid postponing treatment in the hope that the condition will resolve during the convention.

(2) Come with your regular medications
“The wise store up knowledge...” Proverbs 10:14
If you have been diagnosed with any chronic medical condition, such as Hypertension, Diabetes mellitus, Asthma, Epilepsy,
Seizure disorder, Sickle cell disease, Heart disease, and other long-term medical condition

Please come with an adequate supply of all your prescribed medications to last throughout your stay at the convention.
Do not skip your medications because you are fasting or attending spiritual activities without proper medical advice.

(3) Stay safe throughout the convention
“The Lord shall preserve thy going out and thy coming in.” Psalm 121:8
For your safety:
 • Drink plenty of clean water.
 • Observe good hand hygiene.
 • Wash your hands before eating and after using the restroom.
 • Dress according to the weather.
 • Avoid unnecessary exposure to the sun.
 • Eat properly whenever your fasting schedule permits.
 • Report any unusual symptoms early.

(4) Medical services during the convention
By the grace of God, the Clinic Ministry will commence operations on Tuesday, 25 August 2026, to attend to emergency
medical needs throughout the convention.
Qualified medical personnel will be available to provide emergency medical care.

(5) 24-hour emergency medical coverage
Emergency medical services will be available 24 hours daily throughout the convention.
In the event of any medical emergency, kindly contact: Damilare: 08035918156, Gold: 07034764227 and Oluwasesan:
08056438684
Please do not delay in reporting emergencies.

(6) Use the clinic appropriately
“Let all things be done decently and in order.” 1 Cor. 14:40
The clinic is primarily established to attend to medical emergencies and urgent health conditions during the convention.

 ~7~

Kindly avoid visiting the clinic for non-emergency complaints unless referred or advised by the medical team. This will
enable us to respond promptly to genuine emergencies.

(7) Special instructions for pregnant mothers
Pregnant brethren are kindly advised as follows:
If your pregnancy is 33 weeks or less:
 • Come with all your routine medications.
 • Come with your antenatal record.
 • Bring your latest obstetric ultrasound scan report.
If your pregnancy is above 33 weeks (late third trimester):

For your safety, you are strongly encouraged to participate in the convention through the online platform.
However, if attendance at the camp is unavoidable, you must:
 • Report to the clinic immediately upon arrival.
 • Come with a recent obstetric ultrasound scan performed within the last two weeks before the convention.
 • Come with your antenatal records.
 • Bring all prescribed medications.
 • Come with your baby delivery items.
 • Ensure that you have an identified means of transportation should a referral become necessary.

(8) Parents and guardians
“Children are a heritage from the Lord.” Psalm 127:3
 • Supervise your children at all times.
 • Ensure that they remain adequately hydrated.
 • Do not allow children to wander around the camp unattended.
 • Bring medications for children with asthma, allergies, seizures, or other chronic illnesses.
(9) In the event of any medical emergency
 • Do not attempt self-medication for serious conditions.
 • Immediately notify any Clinic Ministry official or call the emergency contacts provided.
 • Early presentation often leads to better outcomes.

Safe fasting guidelines for the convention

A. Preparation for the convention fast
1. Prepare your body gradually
 • Avoid overeating in the days leading up to the fast.
 • Eat balanced meals that include whole grains, lean protein, fruits, vegetables, and healthy fats.

2. Stay well hydrated
 • Increase your water intake in the days before the fast.
 • Limit excessive intake of sugary beverages, as they may contribute to dehydration.

3. Get enough sleep
 • Aim for seven to nine hours of sleep each night before the fasting period.
 • Adequate rest helps the body adjust better to fasting.

4. Plan ahead
 • Schedule demanding physical activities wisely and avoid unnecessary physical exertion.

B. Your disposition during the fast
1. Stay hydrated
 • Kindly ensure that you drink water at the permitted times during the fast.
 • Be alert to possible signs of dehydration, including:
 o Feeling unusually sluggish or tired
 o Dry mouth or a swollen tongue

 ~8~

o Dark yellow or amber-coloured urine
2. Listen to your body
 • Mild hunger may be expected during fasting.
 • However, persistent dizziness, confusion, fainting, chest pain, severe weakness, or heart palpitations should not
 be ignored.
 • Please visit the clinic immediately if you experience any of these symptoms.

3. Conserve your energy
This is especially important for members of the SOP.
 • Avoid strenuous activities and excessive physical play.
 • Gentle walking or stretching may be appropriate.
 • Avoid unnecessary physical and emotional stress.

4. Maximise rest periods
 • Ensure that you rest as much as possible during breaks and designated rest periods.

C. What to do when breaking the fast and after the convention
 • Drink enough water when breaking the fast.
 • Eat the meals provided instead of buying junk food.
 • Do not overeat. This is very important.
 • Avoid excessive amounts of sugary drinks, snacks, and fried foods.

Convention 2026 Welcome Speech
AN EXCEEDING GREAT ARMY. EZEKIEL 37:1-10

Convention 2026 is an exceptional one, where God’s desire is to bring us unto the grace of the beginning. No matter
how far we have gone or how hopeless the situation appears (very dry bones) (Eze 37:11b), He is set to gather us to
Himself, fix every areas / issue such that the outcome does not appear like what had happened to us. Luke 15:22.

The hand of the Lord upon Ezekiel initiated the process, and the mercy of God executed the transformation, as seen
in Prophet Ezekiel’s total submission to God - “O Lord God, thou knowest” (Ezekiel 37:3).

As we have come to this “Boot Camp” where the Lord will be attending to lives and situation, it is very important that
individual aligns with the Lord as we have collectively been doing for the past weeks to accomplish what He wants to
do in raising very dry bones to become exceeding great army. All participants should align daily in fasting, consistent
prayers, intentional attendance of every session with a heart to receive from the Lord. Set your personal expectations
and present them, if confronted with questions, trust in the love and the ability of God to resolve every issue in your
favour and to His glory.

Dry bones shall rise again, this is the assurance that we have from the Lord, nothing else matters, be it in individual
lives, families, fellowships, churches, body of Christ and the Nations. We have come under the exalted hand of the
Lord, that doeth valiantly. (Psalm 118:16-17). Because of the mighty hand of the Lord, all dead situation is reversed
and life is activated in Jesus name. We shall not die but live to declare the works of the Lord.

The voice of the Lord shall visit every situation and non shall escape it, (Psalm 29: 3-11). The majestic power of the
voice of the Lord shall be made manifest, breaking all barriers and limitations to His glory in our lives in Jesus name.

May you experience the breath of the Lord that births life in Jesus name.

You are welcome to the place of encounter with the hand, the voice and the breath of God.

Make this declaration faithfully everyday:
* My dry bones will rise again by the breath of the Lord and I shall live.
* Every dryness – prayerlessness, lack of hunger for God, lack of desire for the Word is broken; I receive fresh
 hunger for God.
* Every broken altar is rebuilt; fire is rekindled; my spirit burns again for the Lord.
* Every dry bone in my life, marriage, home, ministry, academics, career, and business receives a fresh
 visitation from God.
* My local fellowship receives fresh revival fire to raise army for the Lord.
* I arise a repairer of the breach and a restorer of paths to dwell in. I am a builder of the old waste places and
 I raise up the ancient foundations, revival is restored, in Jesus name.
* I shall not disappoint God or waste His investment upon my life at this Convention 2026.
* I am returning with fresh fire, grace, and a renewed commitment to serve His purpose in my local church,
 campus, and community, in Jesus name.

Welcome to Convention 2026

Convention 2026 Bible Study
An Exceeding Great Army
Anchor Verse: “So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon
their feet, an exceeding great army.” (Ezekiel 37:10)

Introduction: From Dry Bones to an Exceeding Great Army
In our anchor text, we see how Ezekiel first saw dry bones that were weak, scattered and without life. Yet God did not
abandon them in that condition. His Word brought order, His breath brought life, and what had been helpless stood as an
exceeding great army. This is a practical manifestation of what true revival is, when the Lord graciously restores dry lives,
corrects what is out of order, renews spiritual strength and raises people who can stand faithfully for Him at their duty
posts in churches, campuses, workplaces and communities.

This prophetic picture of the valley of dry bones speaks directly to TACEF and The African Church. We may have a long
fellowship history, organise many programmes, continue year after year with church outreaches that we call “revival”, and
remain active members for many years, yet our personal altars may have become dry. The Word may no longer govern
our decisions, hidden sinful habits may be growing, and ministry activities may have gradually replaced genuine intimacy
with Christ. When this happens, we need more than another programme; we need the Lord to intervene. We need Him to
breathe upon us again, restore spiritual life, correct what is out of order and raise us from dryness into an exceeding great
army: Spirit-quickened, Word-formed, consecrated, disciplined and mission-ready under the command of Christ.
This study focuses on the making of the army and the character of God’s army, as we apply the learning to our lives so that
each of us produces the real evidence of a revival army in how we live and serve at our respective duty posts.

Opening Discussion
 • What can “dry bones” look like in someone who still claims to be part of a revival army, while actively busy in a
 local fellowship, ministering on the altar or serving regularly in a local church?
 • How can a person be very active for God but gradually lose spiritual life in their secret life? What are the warning
 signals?

Section 1: The Making of the Army
In the process of raising men to serve His purpose in a generation, God does not merely recruit available people but forms
a well-made people He can trust and deploy. Jesus first called the twelve “that they should be with him” before He sent
them to preach (Mark 3:14). There is a “being with Jesus” before the “sending”. God cannot send a life that does not
represent Him because we cannot give what we do not have. Below are the key principles of the divine making of God’s
end-time army:

a. Salvation is the entry and discipleship is the process of divine making for the army: No one is enlisted into Christ’s
 army by church membership, baptism, confirmation, family background, repeated Convention attendance or TACEF
 membership. We must be genuinely born again through repentance and faith in Christ (John 3:3). The saved believer
 must then be discipled, groomed and equipped (Ephesians 2:10; 4:11-13).
b. A consistent personal altar is compulsory for divine use: God is a jealous God, and He will not depend on a life that
 does not know Him or have a continuing relationship with Him. This is where a personal walk with God and a daily altar
 of quiet time, prayer, the Word and holy living come in. A worker may lead prayer, teach, sing or organise programmes
 while personal Bible study and prayer are collapsing. Such a person is becoming unusable as God’s army because
 anyone who does not have a consistent personal walk with God cannot consistently deliver for the Lord as a vessel.
 For if we have not spent time with Him, we have nothing to bring out of our lives. (John 15:4–5; Mark 1:35; Joshua 1:8)
c. An army must win the inner wars before it can win external wars: Sin must have no dominion over a soldier. While
 we can do a lot in spiritual warfare to defeat the enemy, a true soldier focuses on winning the closest battle - the battle
 over sin. Daily victory over ungodly thoughts that are contrary to Christ, daily victory over temptations, and the daily
 discipline of carrying the cross, crucifying the flesh, putting it under and denying self are very important battles that
 every revival soldier must win. In the words of Hebrews 12:4, we must resist sin and win. (Romans 6:12–14; Luke 9:23;
 1 Corinthians 9:27)

 ~ 25 ~

d. Divine grooming of an army: In every nation, soldiers are trained in different ways. They go through rigorous and
 intense routines and rhythms that are demanding and sacrificial. These are the sacrificial routines of an army. For a
 true revival army, there must be a consistent sequence of regular personal retreats, fasting and fasted life, self-denial
 of what is available to others, contentment, learning to survive in the worst places, and living for the sake of others. (1
 Timothy 4:7–8; 1 Corinthians 9:25–27; 2 Timothy 2:3–4)

Discussion
 • Which part of God’s making do Christians most often try to bypass: salvation, discipleship, correction, etc.,
 and why?
 • Why is winning the internal war against sin more important for God’s exceeding great army than just winning
 the external wars?

Section 2: The Character of God’s Army
An army is defined by discipline, loyalty, preparedness, endurance and obedience to the Commander. In the same way,
the evidence that God has revived us will be seen in the kind of people we become afterwards. For by their fruits, we shall
know them. Scripture gives clear marks of a good soldier of Jesus Christ, and some are below:

a. A soldier seeks to please the One who enlisted him: A soldier has only one goal: to please the One who has called him
 to be a soldier. (2 Timothy 2:3). A soldier does not live to please friends, family or colleagues at work. They do not live
 their lives by social trends, as they have only one focus governed by this question: “Will this please Christ?” This
 confronts the desire for self, sin, human applause, titles, social-media validation, peer approval, money or comfort. A
 true soldier is willing to obey Christ even when the decision is unpopular.
b. A soldier refuses entanglement: “No one serving as a soldier gets entangled in civilian affairs” (2 Timothy 2:4 NIV). A
 true revival soldier is not influenced, led or trapped by worldly lifestyles and cultural influences such as endless social
 media, entertainment, unhealthy relationships, money pursuits, betting, pornography, comparison, get rich quick,
 ambition, or any legitimate activity that begins to crowd God out.
c. A soldier endures hardness: A good soldier endures pressure and suffering (2 Timothy 2:3). Being a revival army at our
 duty post may involve opposition, rejection, abuse, disregard, lack of recognition, denial of rights, sacrifice,
 misunderstanding or even little or visible results. In TACEF or The African Church, a revival-minded believer may meet
 resistance while advancing the mandate of revival. Our call to hardness and endurance means remaining faithful at
 our duty post without bitterness, compromise, pride or withdrawal, while seeking wisdom and mature counsel.
d. A soldier is strong in the Lord: Our strength is not in our personal achievements, charisma, education, position, family
 background, experience or human connections, but the Lord (Ephesians 6:10-12). Truth, righteousness, faith, salvation,
 the Word of God and prayer are the sources of strength for the Lord’s army, not how much they can talk, how much
 politics they can play in the church, or even their family background and influence in the local church.
e. A soldier watches, builds and serves others: Every soldier is a watchman who carries others before God and is always
 on watch to provide spiritual defence for others, ensuring that children are not exposed to ungodly living, families are
 protected from sexual perversion, and the church is shielded from satanic doctrines, sinful atmosphere and spiritual
 coldness. A soldier serves in this position through intercession, as they see evil coming and rise to defend as true
 soldiers (Habakkuk 2:1; Ezekiel 33:7).

Discussion
 • Discuss examples of entanglements that distract a soldier in our times and how they can be avoided.
 • As a revival soldier in a local church in The African Church or on a campus, discuss examples of practical areas
 where we must demonstrate hardness and endurance as good soldiers of Christ.
 • Discuss how a true revival soldier can be a watchman who protects the people of God from spiritual decay,
 perversion and pollution.

Personal Reflection
Am I truly alive and growing in Christ, or am I becoming spiritually dry while remaining active in fellowship and ministry? Is
my personal altar of prayer, the Word and holy living consistent? Have I submitted to God’s process of making through
discipleship, correction, obedience, self-denial and spiritual discipline, or am I trying to serve without first being formed?
What inner battles am I still losing? Is sin, distraction, comfort, ambition or the desire to please people weakening my
devotion to Christ? Do I endure hardship as a good soldier, depend on the Lord rather than myself, and remain faithful
when service becomes difficult?

 ~ 26 ~

Am I functioning as a watchman at my present duty post, carrying others in prayer and standing for spiritual life in my
family, fellowship, campus, workplace and church? After this Convention, what specific evidence of revival should become
visible in my life, character, discipline, intercession and service, and who will help me remain accountable?

Conclusion
God did not merely make the dry bones look better; He brought them into life, order and usefulness. Convention 2026
must therefore be a place of encounter where the Lord restores the dry, strengthens the weak, corrects the disordered,
deepens the shallow and breathes afresh upon His people until they stand as an exceeding great army.

For TACEFites, the evidence of a true encounter is seen in genuine conversion, pleasing Him who has called us to be soldiers,
not being entangled with the affairs of this world, winning the inner battle against sin, and being strong in the Lord and
not in ourselves.
Every revival soldier must rise as a watchman with evident fruit: a daily quiet-time person, a disciplined student, a faithful
worker, responsible in the family, a burdened intercessor, a member who strengthens the local fellowship and serve as a
revival agent in The African Church. The army is made before it is useful, and its usefulness is sustained by character.

Closing Prayer Focus

 spiritually alive again.
 • Lord, give me grace to submit fully to Your process of making through discipleship, correction, obedience, prayer,

 • Lord, form in me the character of a faithful soldier of Christ: one who seeks to please You, refuses worldly
 entanglement, endures hardness and draws strength from You alone.
 • Lord, make me a faithful watchman at my duty post, and let the evidence of this Convention be seen in lasting

Assurance of Salvation
Memory Verse: "I write these things to you who believe in the name of the Son of God so that you may know that you
have eternal life" 1 John 5:13.

Key Texts: John 3:16; Ephesians 2:8-9; John 10:27-29; Romans 8:14-17; 1 John 5:11-13; 2 Corinthians 5:17; John 17:3

Seminar Objectives:
 • Understand genuine salvation as the entry point into eternal life and a personal relationship with God through
 repentance and faith in Jesus Christ, beyond religious familiarity or church activities.
 • Distinguish genuine conversion from religious experiences, recognising that baptism, church attendance,
 confirmation ceremony, Convention participation, ministry service, or emotional altar calls do not by themselves
 constitute salvation.
 • Understand the biblical foundation of assurance, including faith in Christ, God's promises, the finished work of
 Christ, the witness of the Holy Spirit, and the evidence of a transformed life.
 • Recognise and respond rightly to doubts, guilt and spiritual struggles, distinguishing the Holy Spirit's conviction
 from condemnation, understanding biblical warnings about falling away, and knowing when to seek help from
 mature believers.
 • Develop a life of confident faith and discipleship through Scripture, prayer, obedience, personal testimony, and
 accountable TACEF fellowship, so that genuine converts are established in their faith rather than repeatedly
 seeking salvation through emotional responses.

Introduction: Salvation is a personal encounter, not guesswork.
Genuine salvation is not meant to be guesswork. It begins with the new birth: a sinner convicted of sin responds to the
gospel in repentance and faith, receives new life in Christ, and begins a transformed direction. It is not merely an emotional
response, a quick verbal confession, or participation in a sinner's prayer at the altar. Jesus said, “You must be born again”
(John 3:7), and Scripture declares that “if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come” (2 Corinthians 5:17).

Many people may have been baptised as infants, confirmed, grown up in The African Church, belonged to TACEF for years,
attended Convention repeatedly, served in the choir or Sunday School, or responded emotionally to altar calls. Yet none
of these automatically equals a personal experience of salvation through repentance and faith in Christ. Salvation is “by
grace... through faith” (Ephesians 2:8-9), and eternal life is to “know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ” (John 17:3).
Religious familiarity must therefore not be mistaken for genuine conversion.

True salvation brings new life in Christ, and that new life should increasingly become visible in holy living, hunger for God
and a changed relationship with sin. It does not mean instant perfection or the absence of temptation, failure or seasons
of doubt. Rather, it marks a new direction: the believer grows in fellowship with God and increasingly becomes like Christ.
This is why Scripture can say, “you may know that you have eternal life” (1 John 5:13).

Key Principles
(1) Understand what genuine salvation means:
Genuine salvation is a personal response to the gospel through repentance and faith in Jesus Christ. It is not merely
becoming religious, morally upright or participating in church activities. Jesus said, “You must be born again” (John 3:7),
and anyone in Christ is a “new creation” (2 Corinthians 5:17).
This is especially important in The African Church, where many may have grown up in church activities and become familiar
with church programmes. Infant baptism, confirmation, years of church membership, repeated TACEF Convention
attendance, service as Sunday School teacher, TACEF membership, or emotional altar calls do not automatically constitute
salvation.

Practical guideline:
 • Repent and believe: Personally turn from sin and place your faith in Christ.
 • Do not substitute familiarity for conversion: Church/TACEF membership, baptism or service cannot save.
 • Know your testimony: Be able to clearly explain how you came to know Christ.
 • Examine your life: Look for evidence of transformation, not merely religious activity. By their fruits we shall know
 them.

 ~ 28 ~

• Settle the matter: If you have never genuinely responded to Christ, do not assume you are saved because you
 have always been among brethren.

(2) Understand what assurance of salvation is and what it is based on:
Assurance is the confidence that, having repented and believed in Christ, we have eternal life according to God's promise.
It rests on Christ's finished work and God's Word, and is confirmed by the witness of the Holy Spirit and the evidence of a
transformed life. “I write these things... so that you may know that you have eternal life” (1 John 5:13; John 10:27-29;
Romans 8:14-17).

Practical guideline:
 • Anchor your assurance in the Word of God: Trust God's Word, not changing feelings.
 • Look to Christ: Remember what He has done rather than constantly measuring your performance.
 • Maintain fellowship with God: Develop a consistent life of quiet time of reading the Bible, prayer and worship.
 • Know God's promises: Meditate on passages such as John 10:27-29 and 1 John 5:11-13.
 • Keep your testimony: Know and remember how you came to Christ and boldly share it.
 • Stay connected: Remain in local fellowship for teaching, encouragement and accountability.
 • Submit to discipleship: Prayerfully identify a mature brother or sister for guidance and accountability.

(3) Recognise the evidence that should accompany genuine conversion:
Genuine salvation produces fruit and a changed life. The believer is not immediately perfect, but there should be growing
evidence of a new relationship with God which will include hunger for His Word, hatred of sin, obedience, love for God's
people, prayer and a desire to become like Christ.
The question is not whether you ever stumble, but whether the direction of your life is toward Christ and growing
obedience. A genuine believer may stumble or fall into sin, but will not deliberately settle into, justify, or make peace with
a life of sin.

Practical checklist for self-examination: Do I genuinely desire fellowship with God? Do I respond to sin with repentance or
justification? Am I increasingly obeying God's Word? Is Christ's character becoming more visible in my life? Am I growing
in love for other believers? Am I becoming spiritually mature, or merely familiar with church and TACEF programmes? Can
those close to me see evidence of Christ's work in my life? Am I accountable to a discipler?

(4) Know how to respond when doubts, guilt and failure come:
Sincere believers may struggle with assurance because of temptation, failure, spiritual immaturity, difficult circumstances
or dependence on feelings. Failure should not make a believer run away from God. “If we confess our sins, he is faithful
and just to forgive us” (1 John 1:9).

Distinguish the conviction of the Holy Spirit from condemnation: Conviction identifies sin and leads to repentance and
restoration, but condemnation drives shame and withdrawal. After honest confession and repentance, do not keep
carrying guilt as though Christ has not forgiven.

Practical guideline:
 • Examine: Identify whether the issue is unconfessed sin, spiritual dryness, fear, failure or dependence on feelings.
 • Confess: Where there is genuine sin, repent, confess it honestly and receive God's forgiveness.
 • Return: After confession, reject self-condemnation and resume obedience and fellowship with God.
 • Seek help: Speak with a mature believer when doubts persist.
 • Remain in fellowship: Do not withdraw because of failure or shame.
 • Stop repeating emotional decisions: If you have genuinely come to Christ, persistent doubt may require Scripture,
 discipleship and accountability, not another altar call.

(5) Distinguish assurance, presumption, temptation, failure, deliberate rebellion and apostasy:
Biblical assurance of salvation is confidence in our relationship with Christ based on His saving work and promises. It must
not be confused with conditions that can weaken, contradict or ultimately reject a genuine walk with Him. Scripture
therefore calls believers to watchfulness, repentance and perseverance.

 ~ 29 ~

Practical distinctions:
 • Temptation: The pressure or desire to sin. Being tempted is not the same as yielding to sin or abandoning Christ;
 resist it and depend on God for victory.
 • Failure: Falling into sin or disobedience. A believer who falls should confess, repent, receive God’s forgiveness and
 return to obedience.
 • Spiritual immaturity: Weakness resulting from limited growth, understanding or discipline. It requires teaching,
 correction, discipleship and deliberate growth.
 • Presumption: Claiming the security of salvation while deliberately ignoring God’s call to holiness. Grace must never
 become an excuse for continuing in sin.
 • Deliberate habitual rebellion: Knowingly choosing and continuing in sin while resisting conviction, correction and
 repentance. Such persistence hardens the heart and places the soul in serious spiritual danger. Repent, forsake
 the rebellion and return to Christ (Hebrews 3:12–13; 1 John 3:6–10).
 • Apostasy: A deliberate rejection or abandonment of Christ and the faith once professed. It is different from
 temptation, doubt or a temporary fall and is treated with the utmost seriousness in Scripture. (Hebrews 10:26–
 29; 2 Peter 2:20–22

(6) Continue and grow in Christ after salvation:
Salvation begins the Christian journey, and it is not the end. Every genuine convert should be connected to a discipler and
local fellowship for follow-up. TACEF must raise believers established in Christ, not people repeatedly making emotional
decisions without spiritual growth.

Practical pathway for continuing in Christ:
 • Daily: Keep a quiet time of worship, Scripture study, prayer and intentional holy living.
 • Weekly: Practise personal fasting; join the TACEF Tuesday fasting and prayer; and seek extended fellowship with
 God for consecration, deeper hunger and the infilling of the Holy Spirit.
 • Monthly: Join the TACEF Covenant Fasting on the first day of the month and set aside time for personal
 consecration.
 • Quarterly: Take a deeper spiritual retreat and assessment through fasting, prayer and honest examination of your
 spiritual walk.
 • Remain in fellowship: Stay connected to your local TACEF fellowship weekly activities and be connected to mature
 TACEF brethren for discipleship and accountability.
 • Practise obedience: Let your assurance produce a transformed life.
 • Seek help early: Do not wait until spiritual struggles become crises. Ask for help on time

Conclusion:
God does not intend His children to live in perpetual uncertainty. “I write these things... so that you may know that you
have eternal life” (1 John 5:13).
Therefore, examine yourself honestly. If you have only inherited a church identity or TACEF membership, settle your
salvation personally now. If you belong to Christ but struggle with doubt, return to His Word. If you fall, repent and return;
if stagnant, seek help and become established. God is raising not merely TACEF members, but a people genuinely alive in
Christ: assured, consecrated, growing and ready for His use.

Building and Maintaining a Disciplined Daily Walk with God
Memory Verse: “Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more
can ye, except ye abide in me.” — John 15:4

Key Texts: Joshua 1:8; Psalm 1:1-3; John 15:4-5; Leviticus 6:13; Luke 5:16; James 1:22; Acts 2:42; Hebrews 10:24-25;
Proverbs 27:17; Hebrews 12:1-2

Seminar Objectives:
 • Understand abiding in Christ as the foundation of a disciplined and fruitful Christian life.
 • Build a daily quiet-time rhythm of Scripture, prayer, worship, meditation and Spirit-led holy living.
 • Develop weekly, monthly and annual spiritual habits that sustain growth beyond special programmes.
 • Recognise and overcome modern enemies of consistency, including digital distraction, poor sleep and ministry
 busyness.
 • Remain accountable through Christian fellowship, discipleship and healthy spiritual relationships.
 • Recover quickly and wisely when spiritual discipline becomes inconsistent or breaks down.

Introduction: A relationship sustained through daily communion
Every building begins with a foundation. In the same way, every Christian life must be built on Jesus Christ (1 Corinthians
3:11). Yet a sound foundation does not remove the need for ongoing spiritual development. A neglected building
deteriorates over time; likewise, a believer who repeatedly neglects prayer, Scripture, holiness and fellowship will
experience spiritual decay and stagnancy.

The Christian life begins with salvation, but it is sustained through abiding in Christ. Jesus did not call His disciples merely
to have occasional encounters with Him; He said, “Abide in me” (John 15:4). Convention, retreats, fellowship time, prayer
meetings and other spiritual gatherings can ignite fresh hunger, but they cannot replace the secret place of one-on-one
fellowship with God as a daily altar fire.

For every TACEFite, disciplined devotion is therefore not an attempt to earn God’s acceptance but a grace-enabled way of
creating regular space for communion with God so that His Word, Spirit and presence increasingly shape our character,
decisions, lifestyle and spiritual fruitfulness.

Key principles
(1) Understand abiding in Christ as the foundation: A disciplined walk with God begins with relationship, not just routine.
Prayer, Bible study, fasting, and meditation are means of remaining attentive and responsive to Christ and they must never
become empty religious activities.

 • Practical guideline for abiding in Christ
 • Make abiding personal: Do not depend on general corporate events like Convention, fellowship programmes or
 another person’s devotion to keep your own spiritual life alive.
 • Keep Christ central: Let every spiritual discipline lead to deeper fellowship with Jesus rather than mere completion
 of a routine.
 • Use the TACEF Read-the-Bible-in-One-Year cycle: Read consistently, but move beyond “What did I read?” to
 “What is God showing me and what must I do?”
 • Watch for spiritual fruit: Growing obedience, holiness, love, humility, spiritual sensitivity and usefulness to God
 are more important than an impressive devotional record.
 • Carry communion into the day: A daily walk with God means remaining responsive to Him in decisions,
 relationships, work, school and service - not only during the quiet-time period.

(2) Build a daily quiet time of the Word, prayer and Spirit-led living: Jesus regularly withdrew to pray (Luke 5:16), showing
that spiritual strength requires intentionality. A quiet time is therefore a protected appointment with God, not a religious
checklist. It should include Scripture, prayer, worship, meditation, memorisation and practical obedience, while remaining
flexible enough for different seasons of life.

 ~ 31 ~

Practical guideline for a daily spiritual rhythm
 • Schedule a realistic appointment: Choose a time and place you can protect consistently rather than copying
 another person’s routine.
 • Engage Scripture prayerfully: Read, study, meditate, record key lessons in a private jotter and identify specific
 applications to your daily walk with God and life routine.
 • Use Scripture memorisation: Participate intentionally in the TACEF Son of Purpose daily memorisation discipline
 so that God’s Word is stored in the heart.
 • Cultivate a balanced prayer life: Include worship, thanksgiving, confession, intercession, personal petitions,
 current ministry burdens and time to listen and respond to God’s leading
 • Practise worship as a lifestyle: Let worship continue beyond the opening and closing of quiet time into the way
 you live through the day.
 • End with obedience: Identify at least one truth to practise, attitude to change, instruction to obey or person to
 respond to, each time you come to the presence of God.

(3) Develop weekly, monthly and annual spiritual habits and rhythms: A healthy spiritual life needs rhythms beyond daily
devotion. Longer periods of fasting, prayer, fellowship, evangelism, reflection and retreat create room for deeper
examination and renewal. These practices should support grace-driven consistency, not become a basis for pride or
comparison.

Suggested measurable spiritual rhythm
 • Daily: Maintain prayer, Scripture, meditation, reflection and practical obedience. Cultivate a life of self-denial and
 spiritual alertness, not merely occasional fasting.
 • Weekly: Participate in TACEF Tuesday fasting and prayer, remain active in local fellowship, make a deliberate
 evangelistic effort and create a longer period for prayer or Bible study.
 • Monthly: Conduct a personal spiritual review and, where possible, include an extended period of prayer, fasting
 or retreat.
 • Annually: Complete a Bible-reading cycle, take a personal retreat, review recurring weaknesses, and set clear
 priorities for spiritual growth.
 • After Convention and major spiritual gatherings: Write down major convictions and decisions, then translate
 them into daily and weekly practices so that spiritual encounters become sustained habits.

(4) Overcome modern enemies of consistency: One of the greatest challenges to spiritual discipline today is the
competition for attention. Phones now function as communication platforms, entertainment centres, classrooms,
workplaces and newsrooms. Endless WhatsApp activity, social media, streaming, late-night browsing, work pressure,
commuting, school demands, parenting responsibilities and even ministry busyness can quietly crowd out the secret place.

Practical guideline for protecting the secret place
 • Create phone-free periods: Keep notifications and unnecessary digital activity away from prayer and Bible-study
 time. Do not be praying and at the same time playing with your phone.
 • Do not begin every day with your phone: Allow God’s Word and prayer to shape the first part of the day before
 social-media traffic takes over.
 • Protect sleep: Repeated late-night browsing and entertainment can destroy morning devotion and weaken
 concentration.
 • Build devotion around real life: A student, parent, commuter and shift worker may need different schedules. The
 principle is deliberate, protected communion with God, not one rigid timetable.
 • Control entertainment and social-media use: Set practical boundaries around WhatsApp, Instagram, TikTok,
 YouTube, streaming and other attention-consuming platforms.
 • Do not let ministry replace intimacy: Bible reading only for a sermon, teaching or fellowship assignment is not the
 same as feeding your own soul.

 ~ 32 ~

(5) Remain accountable in Christian fellowship: God did not design the Christian life to be lived in isolation. TACEF
fellowship provides encouragement, correction, and shared spiritual burdens. Mature disciplers and trusted believers can
also ask the questions that public Christian activity often hides: How is your prayer life? Are you still in the Word? What
temptation keeps returning? Are you obeying what God has shown you?

Practical guideline for healthy accountability
 • Remain active in local TACEF fellowship: Do not allow work, relocation, marriage, school transition or ministry
 responsibility to quietly disconnect you from fellowship.
 • Participate in fellowship spiritual rhythms: Carry current ministry prayer burdens and serve responsibly rather
 than remaining a spectator.
 • Maintain a discipler or mature-believer relationship: Allow someone trustworthy to ask honest questions and
 provide biblical correction.
 • Choose accountability wisely: Look for honesty, wisdom, spiritual maturity and healthy boundaries; same-gender
 accountability is generally the safer model for personal spiritual matters.
 • Do not pretend: Accountability becomes useful only when the real struggles, inconsistencies and temptations can
 be discussed honestly.
 • Stay connected to the wider fellowship: Private devotion and corporate worship strengthen one another; neither
 should replace the other.

(6) Recover quickly when spiritual discipline breaks down: Even sincere believers can experience seasons of inconsistency.
There may be missed prayer times, irregular Bible study, travel, exhaustion, distraction or sin that damages fellowship with
God. The danger is allowing one missed day to become a new pattern and then allowing shame to make returning to God
feel harder. Spiritual maturity includes learning how to return quickly and rebuild wisely.

Practical guideline for recovery
 • Return immediately: Do not wait for Monday, a new month, Convention or another special programme before
 beginning again with miss your spiritual rhythm.
 • Identify the real cause: Was the breakdown caused by sin, poor sleep, an unrealistic schedule, phone distraction,
 travel, discouragement, work pressure or family demands?
 • Remove practical roadblocks: Reorganise time, reduce distractions, repair sleep patterns or seek help where
 necessary.
 • Repent where sin is involved: Confess honestly, receive God’s forgiveness and return to obedience rather than
 remaining in condemnation.
 • Reconnect with accountability: If the pattern keeps returning, speak with your discipler or a mature believer and
 agree on practical next steps.

Conclusion: Abiding in Christ is the secret of a fruitful spiritual life
A strong spiritual life does not happen accidentally. It is sustained through abiding in Christ, Scripture, prayer, holiness,
fellowship, accountability and dependence on the Holy Spirit. Every TACEFite must therefore examine not only the altar
displayed publicly, but the private altar nobody sees: the Word we read when nobody is asking, the prayers we pray when
nobody is leading, the sins we reject when nobody would know and the obedience we practise when there is no applause.

The goal is not a perfect timetable but a life that keeps returning to Christ and growing in communion, holiness and
obedience. Let nothing detach you from Christ, abide in Him, be rooted in His grace and find expression in the daily altar
of encounter with God because, “the fire shall ever be burning upon the altar; it shall never go out” (Leviticus 6:13).

Becoming God's Trusted Discipler and Builder of Men
Memory Verse: “And the things that thou hast heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men,
who shall be able to teach others also.” 2 Timothy 2:2

Key Texts: Matthew 28:19-20; Mark 3:14; 1 Corinthians 11:1; 2 Timothy 2:2; 2 Timothy 3:16-17; Hebrews 5:12-14; Titus
2:1-8

Seminar Objectives:
 • Understand biblical discipleship as helping people become mature followers of Christ, not followers of the
 discipler.
 • Understand the character, trust, confidentiality and boundaries required before being entrusted with another
 person’s spiritual formation.
 • Establish a practical and accountable one-to-one discipleship rhythm that helps a believer grow in Christ and in
 everyday life.
 • Raise disciples who become thoroughly furnished for every good work and increasingly capable of discipling
 others.

Introduction: God desires multiplication through transformed lives
God’s purpose has always included multiplication. He created humanity in His image and called people to reflect His
character and purposes in the earth. Jesus later demonstrated this through discipleship: He called people to be with Him,
taught them, corrected them, entrusted them with responsibility and prepared them to carry the gospel beyond His
physical presence.

TACEF therefore cannot fulfil a revival mandate by gathering people around programmes alone. Revival must be
reproduced in lives. Mature believers must intentionally help younger believers become rooted in Christ, disciplined in
spiritual life, sound in character, effective in service and capable of helping others grow. Yet this responsibility must be
handled carefully because discipleship can become unhealthy when a discipler begins to seek ownership, unquestioning
loyalty or personal dependence.
The disciple belongs to Jesus Christ. A trusted discipler is therefore a steward, not an owner; a guide, not a “mini-god”; an
example, not the final voice of God in another person’s life. The question is not merely whether we can teach others, but
whether God can trust us to build lives without manipulating them.

Key principles
(1) Understand biblical discipleship: we make disciples of Christ, not followers of ourselves: Biblical discipleship is an
intentional relationship in which a more mature believer helps another believer grow through Scripture, example, prayer,
accountability, correction and service. Jesus modelled this by calling the Twelve “that they should be with him” before
sending them out (Mark 3:14). Paul could also say, “Be ye followers of me, even as I also am of Christ” (1 Corinthians 11:1).
The discipler’s authority is therefore always limited by Christ and Scripture.

Practical guideline for Christ-centred discipleship
 • Point continually to Christ: Every lesson, correction and counsel should help the disciple know, obey and depend
 on Jesus rather than become dependent on the discipler.
 • Be a disciple before discipling others: Keep your own prayer life, Bible study, holiness, accountability and
 obedience current to be a true example worth following.
 • Treat discipleship as stewardship, not ownership: The person belongs to Christ. You are temporarily entrusted to
 help that life mature.
 • Model what you teach: Let the disciple see consistency between your public teaching and private conduct.
 • Aim for maturity and multiplication: Successful discipleship should increasingly produce a believer who can study
 Scripture, make responsible decisions under God, serve others and eventually disciple another person.

 ~ 34 ~

(2) Become a trusted discipler through character, confidentiality and healthy boundaries: A discipler is not merely
someone with knowledge but someone whose life is safe enough to influence another person for the Lord. Trust is built
over time through faithfulness, humility, confidentiality, gentleness and example. It must never be extracted through
pressure, fear, guilt, spiritual intimidation or claims such as “God told me you must obey me.” Healthy discipleship produces
increasing dependence on Christ, not increasing personal control by the discipler.

Safeguards and practical boundaries
 • Do not become a “mini-god”: Never demand total loyalty, insist on being part of every decision or behave as
 though the disciple needs your permission to obey God.
 • Prefer same-gender discipleship: Brothers discipling brothers and sisters discipling sisters should normally remain
 the preferred model.
 • Maintain marital transparency: Married disciplers should keep appropriate transparency with their spouses and
 avoid secret or emotionally intimate relationships with disciples.
 • Use appropriate meeting places and times: Avoid situations that create unnecessary emotional, moral or
 reputational risk.
 • Protect confidentiality: Information shared in confidence must not later be used to embarrass, threaten, control
 or win an argument.
 • Maintain clear financial boundaries: Do not create emotional or financial dependency, borrow from a disciple, or
 use spiritual influence to obtain personal support.
 • Do not isolate the disciple: Encourage healthy relationships with family, local TACEF fellowship, and other mature
 believers.
 • Know the limits of your role: Refer medical, mental-health, safeguarding, legal or other specialised matters to
 appropriate pastoral or professional support when necessary.

(3) Establish a practical one-to-one discipleship rhythm: Discipleship requires more than occasional counselling or
informal conversation. It is intentional and sustained investment in a life. Begin in prayer, establish a clear and healthy
relationship, agree on a realistic meeting rhythm, review previous commitments and allow the word of God to address
both spiritual life and everyday conduct. Accountability should be agreed and purposeful, not imposed as control.

A practical discipleship meeting can review
 • Salvation and relationship with Christ: Is the disciple established in the gospel and growing in assurance, prayer
 and Bible reading?
 • Character and victory over sin: What recurring temptations, attitudes, habits or relationships require repentance,
 discipline or support?
 • Fellowship and relationships: Is the disciple active in local fellowship, relating well with family and building healthy
 Christian relationships?
 • Academics, career, work and finances: Is Christian diligence, integrity and responsibility visible outside the prayer
 room?
 • Evangelism, ministry gifts and service: Is the disciple learning to witness, serve and use God-given capacities
 responsibly?
 • Current challenges and previous commitments: What was agreed at the last meeting, what progress has been
 made and what practical next step is required?

Practical rhythm for the discipler
 • Pray before and after meetings: Ask God for wisdom, discernment and grace rather than relying on experience
 alone.
 • Listen before correcting: Understand the situation clearly and avoid making assumptions.
 • Use Scripture responsibly: Do not weaponise Bible verses to force compliance; explain truth and help the disciple
 respond to God.
 • Share life as appropriate: Discipleship includes example, service and ordinary moments, not only formal lessons.
 However, be led on what to share or what not to share
 • Give increasing responsibility: Allow the disciple to serve, make responsible decisions and learn from experience
 without possessiveness.
 • Review progress periodically: Ask whether the disciple is becoming more like Christ, more responsible, more
 discerning and less dependent on constant supervision.

 ~ 35 ~

(4) Become thoroughly furnished unto every good work: from discipleship to every life expression: Discipleship is
incomplete if it produces a person who can pray and quote Scripture but remains careless, dishonest, lazy, or ineffective
in everyday responsibilities. Scripture describes the mature believer as “throughly furnished unto all good works” (2
Timothy 3:17). The discipler should therefore help the disciple carry Christlike character into studies, career or business,
finances, family relationships, ministry gifts, service and public conduct.

 • Practical guideline for whole-life discipleship
 • Connect spiritual growth to daily responsibility: Prayer, holiness and Scripture should increasingly shape
 punctuality, diligence, truthfulness, relationships, academic excellence and work ethic.
 • Direct the disciple to relevant development platforms: Where appropriate, connect growing believers to TACEF
 support platforms around academics, professional development, finance, ministry gifts and spiritual disciplines.
 • Prepare the disciple to disciple others: 2 Timothy 2:2 describes a multiplying chain - what has been received
 should eventually be committed to other faithful people.
 • Celebrate maturity, not dependency: A discipler should rejoice when the disciple can study Scripture, hear and
 obey God responsibly, make wise decisions and serve others without constant supervision.

Conclusion: Trusted with lives for the sake of Christ
The Lord is looking for mature believers He can trust with people. Such disciplers are not merely gifted or available; they
are accountable, safe, confidential, teachable and deeply committed to Christ. They do not build private kingdoms or
loyalty systems. They build people who increasingly know Jesus, obey Scripture, live responsibly and become capable of
strengthening others.

TACEF will multiply revival most sustainably when every mature soldier sees discipleship as a stewardship: receiving people
from Christ, helping them grow, releasing them into responsible service and preparing them to build others. “The same
commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also” (2 Timothy 2:2).

 ~ 36 ~

Raising Godly Children Through Children’s Ministry and Sunday School
Memory Verse: “Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.” Proverbs 22:6
Key Texts: Deuteronomy 6:6–9; Psalm 78:4–7; Matthew 18:1–6; Matthew 19:14; 2 Timothy 3:14–15; John 21:15

Seminar Objectives:
 • Understand Children’s Church and Sunday School as a strategic mission field for salvation, discipleship and revival
 among the next generation.
 • Recognise the urgent weaknesses in many children’s ministries today, including inconsistent teachers,
 inadequate age-grade engagement and the use of entertainment in place of spiritual formation.
 • Develop a deliberate discipleship pathway that continues beyond Sunday through prayer, Bible engagement,
 TACEF Seed of Purpose and family follow-up.
 • Understand the spiritual discipline, discernment, safeguarding boundaries and preparation required of every
 children’s teacher.
 • Raise children who make a personal decision for Jesus, grow in biblical truth and become young agents of revival
 in The African Church.

Introduction: Children’s Church is a mission field, not a childcare room
Children are among the most impressionable members of the church. Their hearts are like a clean writing surface on which
family, school, media, friends and the church are continually making impressions. What is written early can shape what
they believe about God, themselves and the Christian faith for many years. For this reason, Children’s Church must never
be treated merely as a place to keep children quiet while adults worship. The present reality in many parishes of The African
Church makes this assignment especially urgent. Some children do not have consistent teachers. In some churches there
are too few workers to provide meaningful age-grade engagement. Others depend almost entirely on elderly mothers who
may be willing and available but have not been sufficiently equipped for the developmental and spiritual needs of different
age groups. In some places, children are simply shown cartoons or given activities mainly to keep them seated and quiet.
This may occupy children, but it does not necessarily disciple them.

The challenge becomes deeper because some children may also observe things happening in the adult church like church
tensions, unguarded statements, disrespect for spiritual things or other conduct that contradicts what they are being
taught about Christ. There are also many whose parents do not attend the church regularly, some are from homes that do
not maintain a family altar or do not consistently model Christian living at home, Children’s Church is therefore their
strongest pathway to knowing the Lord. The teacher must therefore see every child as a soul to be won, a life to be discipled
and a possible instrument of future revival.

Key principles
(1) Restore Children’s Church to its true spiritual purpose: Jesus said, “Suffer the little children to come unto me...” (Mark
10:14). The first task is therefore not to entertain children but to bring them deliberately to Christ. A successful Children’s
Church is not one where children merely remain quiet but a place where they are steadily learning Scripture, praying,
understanding salvation, growing in obedience and developing a real relationship with Jesus.

Practical guideline for restoring the spiritual purpose
 • Make salvation central: Teach the Gospel clearly and repeatedly in age-appropriate language. Do not assume
 that a child is saved simply because the parents are Christians or because the child has grown up in church.
 • Seek definite spiritual decisions: Create opportunities for children to understand sin, repentance, faith in Christ
 and assurance of salvation. Follow up those who make commitments rather than treating the moment as the end
 of the process.
 • Replace activities with discipleship: Games, songs, creative learning and carefully selected media may support
 teaching, but they must never replace prayer, Scripture, worship, and personal spiritual engagement.
 • Raise revival-minded children: Help children see that they can pray, witness to friends, obey God, serve others
 and become examples for Christ now, not only when they become adults.

 ~ 37 ~

(2) Build a consistent, sufficient and age-appropriate teaching team: Children of different ages do not learn, reason or
respond in the same way. A single undifferentiated class may make genuine discipleship difficult. Part of your effort is to
intentionally raise enough teachers and helpers so that children receive consistent care and age-appropriate engagement.

Practical guideline for building the teaching workforce
 • Treat teaching as a calling, not a roll-call duty: Children need teachers who are consistent, spiritually prepared
 and emotionally present, not workers who appear only when their names are on a roster.
 • Create age-grade groups where possible: Organise children into practical developmental bands so that Bible
 explanations, questions, activities and expectations match their level of understanding.
 • Recruit and train more workers: Do not leave the entire ministry to a few old mothers or long-serving volunteers.
 Deliberately identify younger adults, parents and spiritually mature brethren who can be trained to serve
 alongside experienced workers.
 • Use experienced mothers wisely: Value their maturity, patience and spiritual experience, while also
 strengthening the team with workers who can support lesson design, age-grade facilitation, technology and
 contemporary child engagement.
 • Build continuity: Keep basic records of lessons, attendance, salvation decisions, follow-up needs and teacher
 assignments so that children do not experience a completely different ministry every Sunday.

(3) Disciple the child beyond Sunday morning: Deuteronomy 6:6–9 presents spiritual formation as an ongoing life process,
not a once-a-week event. Few hours on Sunday is rarely enough to counter the many influences children encounter during
the rest of the week. Children’s ministry must therefore establish a simple discipleship rhythm that continues between
Sundays.

Practical guideline for weekday discipleship
 • Give simple weekly spiritual assignments: Provide age-appropriate Bible reading, memory verses, prayer points,
 short reflection questions or acts of obedience that children can complete before the next Sunday.
 • Connect children to TACEF Seed of Purpose: Encourage regular participation in the TACEF Seed of Purpose
 fellowship every Saturday at 6pm. Where direct participation is difficult, families should use the available pre-
 recorded Mixlr connection to listen after the session.
 • Use the 7-Pillar framework: Apply the TACEF Seed of Purpose 7-Pillar teaching framework as a structured
 pathway for helping them grow in balanced Christian character and discipleship.
 • Pray for children by name: Teachers should maintain a prayer burden for the children under their care, especially
 those showing spiritual, behavioural, family or emotional concerns.
 • Integrate them into TACEF fellowship life: As appropriate, intentionally connect children to local TACEF
 fellowship activities so that their spiritual development does not depend on one Sunday class alone.

(4) Become a watchman, shepherd and spiritual parent: A children’s teacher needs more than lesson notes. The teacher
requires discernment to understand the spiritual condition of children, wisdom to respond to difficult situations and the
heart of a shepherd who cares deeply for each child. “Feed my lambs” (John 21:15) is a serious pastoral responsibility.

Practical guideline for spiritual watchfulness and safeguarding
 • Observe beyond behaviour: Do not label a restless, withdrawn, aggressive or unusually quiet child too quickly.
 Pray and seek wisdom about what may be happening in the child’s life.
 • Discern harmful influences: Be alert to materials, conversations, games, media, objects or ideas children may
 bring into the Sunday school that could negatively influence others. Address concerns calmly, wisely and through
 appropriate church and parent channels.
 • Maintain clear relational boundaries: Show warmth and godly affection without creating secret, exclusive or
 emotionally dependent relationships, especially with older children. Keep counselling and communication
 transparent and follow sound safeguarding practices.
 • Never use spiritual authority carelessly: Do not shame, threaten or manipulate children in the name of discipline.
 Correct with firmness, love, dignity and age-appropriate wisdom.
 • Escalate serious concerns responsibly: Where a child discloses or displays a significant welfare or safety concern,
 involve the appropriate leadership and responsible adults rather than attempting to manage the matter secretly
 or alone.

 ~ 38 ~

(5) Prepare spiritually and professionally for every session: A teacher should not arrive on Sunday and begin looking for
what to teach. Children quickly recognise whether a teacher is prepared, interested and spiritually engaged. Excellence in
preparation communicates that their souls matter.

Practical guideline for effective session preparation
 • Pray before you teach: Pray for the lesson, the children and specific needs. Ask the Holy Spirit for understanding,
 compassion, discernment and a clear burden for the session.
 • Study the Bible personally: Do not depend only on a lesson manual. Understand the Scripture yourself so that
 you can explain it faithfully, answer questions and avoid passing errors to children.
 • Prepare learning materials early: Have Bible passages, memory verses, visual aids, activities, songs and other
 teaching resources ready before the class begins.
 • Engage rather than lecture: Use questions, demonstrations, repetition, stories, participation, small-group
 activities and practical examples that help children connect biblical truth to everyday life.
 • Manage the class with purpose: Create an orderly, welcoming and joyful environment where every child can
 participate without allowing entertainment to become the main objective.
 • Review and improve: After each session, ask what the children understood, what did not work, which children
 need follow-up and what should change before the next meeting.

(6) Labour with parents and raise children as agents of revival: The church cannot disciple children effectively while
completely ignoring the home. Teachers may need to partner with parents as the Lord may lead and provides opportunity.

Practical guideline for parent partnership and revival formation
 • Follow up intentionally: Where a child is repeatedly absent, spiritually troubled or making significant progress,
 prayerfully engage the parents or guardians through appropriate channels rather than allowing the child to
 disappear unnoticed.
 • Encourage the family altar: Help parents understand the value of simple home prayer, Bible reading, worship
 and Christian conversation. Provide practical ideas that families can actually sustain.
 • Do not condemn struggling parents: Some parents may themselves be spiritually weak or inconsistent. Approach
 them with humility, prayer and a desire to help rather than superiority or accusation.
 • Celebrate and nurture spiritual growth: Recognise children who memorise Scripture, show Christlike conduct or
 take steps of obedience. Use encouragement to strengthen genuine growth, not competition.
 • Prepare them for transition: Do not allow children to disappear spiritually when they outgrow Children’s Church.
 Create intentional pathways into the local TACEF fellowship.
 • See every child as a potential revival vessel: Labour until children do more than know Bible stories. Pray that
 they know Christ personally, love His Word, walk in purity, influence their friends and become part of the revival
 army God is raising.

Conclusion:
The great need of The African Church is not simply for more Children’s Church activities but for spiritually alive teachers
who will labour for the salvation and discipleship of the next generation. The children before us are receiving impressions
every day from the home, school, media, friends and the church. We must therefore refuse to hand their spiritual formation
over to cartoons, occasional volunteers or unstructured Sunday activities.

God is looking for teachers who will see themselves as watchmen, shepherds and spiritual parents, that is, teachers who
pray, prepare, study, discern, protect, follow up and remain consistent. They will build age-appropriate learning, partner
with God, connect children to TACEF Seed of Purpose and local fellowship, and continue the discipleship process beyond
Sunday morning.

Our goal is not merely well-behaved children during service but children who have made a personal decision for Jesus,
maintain a growing prayer life, understand Christian character and become young agents of revival. Every child faithfully
discipled today can become a voice for Christ in the family, school, church and generation tomorrow.
“We will not hide them from their children, shewing to the generation to come the praises of the Lord...” Psalm 78:4
