Introduction
This week brings us to Jericho, the first major fortified city Israel confronted after crossing Jordan. Jericho stood between
the people of God and the practical possession of the Promised land. It was not merely a city; it was a stronghold. The Bible
says, “Now Jericho was straitly shut up because of the children of Israel: none went out, and none came in.” From the natural
point of view, Jericho was closed, defended, resistant, and inaccessible. Yet, before any wall fell, before any shout was
raised, and before any weapon was lifted, the Lord had already spoken victory to Joshua: “See, I have given into thine hand
Jericho.” This means that the battle was not first decided by what Israel could see, but by what God had said.

God’s method for taking Jericho was unusual. Israel was not instructed to attack the wall with best of military weapons.
They were commanded to march round the city in silence, follow the ark, allow the priests to blow the trumpets, and shout
only at the appointed time. This teaches that spiritual victory is not secured by human formula or copied methods. Human
strategies are useful, and learning from others is important, but knowing God’s method for every season is much more
important for a sustained life of victory. The fall of Jericho teaches us that God’s battle must be won God’s way.
.
Ephesians gives us a deeper meaning of this warfare. Paul teaches that we are not wrestling against flesh and blood, but
against principalities, powers, rulers of the darkness of this world, and spiritual wickedness in high places. Jericho therefore
becomes a powerful picture of the strongholds that stand against the salvation of souls, the restoration of families, the
revival of local churches, the transformation of campuses, and the reclaiming of communities for the Lord. Behind many
closed lives, resistant families, spiritually cold churches, and hardened territories are unseen forces that must be confronted
through warfare prayer, faith, the Word of God, and the whole armour of God. Therefore, the battle for souls is not only a
matter of preaching; it is also a matter of spiritual warfare. We must preach, teach, disciple, and follow up , but we must
also pray until the strongholds holding lives and destinies are broken. There are walls that preaching alone cannot break.
There are gates that human wisdom alone cannot open. There are powers that only bow when God’s people stand in the
strength of the Lord. Dear TACEFites, if we must see Jericho fall, we must be strong in the Lord, put on the whole armour
of God, and win God’s battle God’s way.

Teachings
1. Victory Begins from Divine Promise, Not Visible Result: The first thing Scripture tells us about Jericho is that it was
“straitly shut up.” Nobody went out, and nobody came in. The city was fortified, defended, and resistant. From the natural
point of view, Jericho was inaccessible. Yet, the Lord said to Joshua, “See, I have given into thine hand Jericho.” This means
that God’s promise can already be sure, even when the way forward still looks closed and impossible. Jericho was locked
against Israel on earth, but God had already handed it over to them in heaven.

This is very important for every revival move. A person may look hardened, but that does not mean grace cannot reach
them. A family may look resistant, but that does not mean God cannot save them. A local church may look dry, but that
does not mean revival cannot come. A campus may appear captured by sin, cultism, immorality, worldliness, and rebellion,
but that does not mean the Lord cannot raise witnesses there. A workplace may appear corrupt, hostile, and spiritually
closed, but Christ can still be represented there.

God did not first ask Joshua to focus on the wall. He asked him to “see” what heaven had already given. This was not
ordinary sight; it was faith-shaped vision. Joshua had to see victory before stepping out in faith. He had to believe God’s
promise before the wall fell. He had to lead the people from the assurance of what God had spoken, not from the fear of
what the city looked like. Dear TACEFites, we must not allow shut gates to cancel divine promises in our hearts. Some
territories God has assigned to us may first appear impossible. Some souls God wants to save may first appear difficult.

 ~ 120 ~

Some assignments God has placed before us may look too hard. But if God has spoken, the wall will definitely fall. The
possessing army must not only see walls; it must see the Lord who has already declared victory.

2. God’s Strategy May Look Foolish to Men, but Obedience Wins: The strategy God gave Joshua did not look like normal
military wisdom. There were no siege engines and no physical attack on the wall. The people were commanded to march
round the city once each day for six days. On the seventh day, they were to march round the city seven times. The priests
were to blow the trumpets, and the people were to shout only when Joshua commanded them. To natural men, this method
may have looked slow, foolish, or ineffective. Yet, it carried divine authority because it came from God. This teaches us that
spiritual victory is not by human formula, but by obedience to God’s strategy. The fall of Jericho fell because Israel obeyed
God’s complete instructions. The shout had power because it came at the appointed time, after the appointed process, in
obedience to the appointed word of God.
Many believers want to copy methods without seeking God. Learning from others is good, but copying without spiritual
discernment can become dangerous. What God used in one place may not be His exact method for another place. What
worked in one season may not be the strategy for the next season. This is important for each of us as we see walls of Jericho
fall in our careers, ministry, family, calling, academics and marriage. Sometimes God’s method will require silence when we
want to speak. Sometimes it will require patience when we want speed. Sometimes it will require repeated obedience
when we want instant results. Sometimes it will require praise before the wall falls. The method may look foolish to men,
but if it is from God and obeyed fully, strongholds will fall.

3. Complete Obedience, Patient Faith, and Praise as Warfare: The command to march round Jericho required complete
and patient obedience. Israel had to march once a day for six days without seeing visible results. They had to return to the
camp after each march, while the wall still stood. On the seventh day, they had to march seven times before the shout
came. This means that victory did not come through hurried obedience, partial obedience, or emotional impatience. It
came through complete obedience to God’s order. If Israel had marched for three or five days and stopped, the wall would
still have stood. If they had shouted before the appointed time, they would have disobeyed. If they had changed God’s
method because it looked too slow, they would have missed the miracle. This connects with the truth that knowing God
must produce obedience as we learned in our 2025/2026 study series. Obedience is not only proved when the instruction
is exciting; it is proved when it is inconvenient and not yet producing visible results.

The shout at Jericho was also important. Joshua said, “Shout; for the LORD hath given you the city.” This was not ordinary
noise. It was not entertainment. It was not emotional display. It was not an attempt to excite the people. It was a shout of
faith released in obedience to God’s instruction. Praise becomes warfare when it flows from faith, obedience, revelation,
and confidence in God’s Word. We also need to note that the children of Israel did not use praise to replace obedience.
They marched as commanded, kept silent as commanded, and shouted when commanded. This is a major lesson for the
Lord’s army. Our singing must not become entertainment. Our shouting must not become noise without obedience and
our worship must not become performance without surrender. But when praise rises from a life that believes God, obeys
God, and stands on His promise, it becomes a weapon of warfare.

4. Jericho as a Picture of Strongholds - Understanding Warfare Principles: Jericho was not only a physical city; it was a
picture of a stronghold resisting God’s people from entering into inheritance. It was shut, fortified, defended, and opposed
to the progress of Israel. In the New Testament, Ephesians 6 helps us understand that behind many visible oppositions and
attacks are unseen spiritual forces. Paul says, “For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against
powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.” This means the battle
for souls, families, local churches, campuses, communities, and nations is spiritual and the book of Ephesians gave us the 4
layers of these forces as below:
• Principalities. These speak of organised spiritual authorities and ruling structures of darkness that influence territories,
 systems, cultures, and generations against the purpose of God. They represent higher levels of demonic ordering that
 seek to keep people, communities, institutions, and territories under spiritual blindness and rebellion. In the Jericho
 picture, principalities can be seen as the organised resistance that keeps an entire city shut against God’s purpose.
• Powers. These refer to forces that exercise authority, oppression, control, and bondage over lives and destinies. They
 can manifest through addictions, fear, lust, pride, bitterness, unbelief, ancestral bondage, false worship, and patterns
 that keep people from responding to the gospel. In the Jericho picture, powers are like the strength behind the gates
 and walls that prevent access and hold the inhabitants under bondage.
• The rulers of the darkness of this world. These are forces that promote darkness, deception, corruption, sin, moral
 confusion, and rebellion in the systems of this world. They influence minds, values, behaviours, and social patterns so

 ~ 121 ~

that darkness appears normal and truth appears strange. In the Jericho picture, they are like the atmosphere of the
 city itself, a territory organised around resistance to God’s rule and opposed to the light of His people.
• Spiritual wickedness in high places. This speaks of deeper spiritual operations that oppose worship of God, holiness,
 truth, prayer, revival, and the knowledge of God. These forces seek to corrupt altars, pollute worship, weaken spiritual
 authority, frustrate intercession, and resist the purposes of God from unseen realms. In the Jericho picture, this
 represents the hidden spiritual force behind the visible wall, the unseen wickedness strengthening the visible
 resistance.

This is why every army of the Lord must be ready for spiritual warfare. The people we are trying to win are not our enemies.
The real battle is against the strongholds and spiritual forces that hold lives and destinies in bondage. Therefore, salvation
is beyond preaching alone; it requires prayer. Revival is beyond organising programmes alone; it requires warfare. We must
preach the gospel, but we must also pray until veils are removed, gates are opened, strongholds are pulled down, and the
light of Christ shines into hearts.

Step-by-Step Applications and Practical Implications
• See beyond closed gates: Identify one area of your life, family, local church, campus, workplace, or community that
 looks shut. Begin to pray from the assurance of God’s Word and not from the fear of visible resistance.
• Seek God’s method, not copied formulas: Before starting any plan, investment, programme, outreach, ministry effort,
 family decision, relationship step, business move, or major life decisions, ask the Lord for His specific strategy.
• Obey fully and patiently: Write down one instruction God has already given you that you have obeyed only halfway.
 Return to it with humility and complete the obedience.
• Practise disciplined silence: Joshua commanded the people not to speak until the appointed time. This week, watch
 your words. Refuse murmuring, negative confession, careless talk, and unbelieving speech.
• Turn praise into warfare: Praise God from faith, not entertainment. Spend 1 full hour this week to sing, worship, and
 thank Him over situations that have not yet changed, because His promise is greater than the wall.
• Pray against strongholds: Choose specific names, families, locations, or issues and invest prayer into them. Ask God to
 pull down every stronghold resisting salvation, holiness, revival, discipleship, and divine purpose.
• Do not fight people as enemies: Remember that we wrestle not against flesh and blood. Speak to people with love but
 confront strongholds in prayer.
Questions for Discussion

 Israel could not enter it?
 2. What does Jericho teach us about strongholds that resist the salvation of souls, revival, and territorial possession?
 3. Why must TACEFites seek God’s method instead of relying only on copied formulas and personal ideas?
 4. What does the silence, marching, trumpet, and shout teach us about complete obedience and divine timing?
 5. How can praise become warfare, and how can it become mere entertainment?
 6. Why must soul-winning, discipleship, and revival work be backed by prayer and spiritual warfare?

Personal Reflection
Am I discouraged because the gates look shut, or am I standing on what God has spoken? Do I see my family, local church,
campus, workplace, career, finance, community, and nation only through the walls of resistance, or through the promise of
God? Do I seek God’s method before taking action, or do I rely on copied formulas, human intelligence, and personal ideas?
Have I obeyed God fully, or am I giving Him partial obedience while expecting complete victory? Am I patient enough to
keep marching when there is no visible result yet? Is my praise rooted in faith and obedience, or is it only emotional
excitement? Do I understand that the people I want to win are not my enemies, but souls under strongholds that must be
pulled down by prayer? Am I putting on the whole armour of God, or am I trying to fight spiritual battles with fleshly
methods?

Prayer Points

Introduction
Our study this week brings us to one of the most sobering moments in Israel’s journey of possession. After the mighty fall
of the wall of Jericho, Israel moved towards a small city called Ai (not AI - Artificial Intelligence) with confidence. Ai looked
smaller and easier than Jericho. The spies even advised Joshua that only a few thousand men needed to go, because the
city was not as intimidating as Jericho. Yet Israel suffered defeat before a smaller enemy. The hearts of the people melted,
Joshua fell before the ark of the Lord, and the whole camp was thrown into confusion. The defeat at Ai was not because
God had become weak. It was not because Ai was stronger than Israel, but it was because there was hidden sin in the camp.

The story of Achan teaches us that secret sin can bring open defeat. One Israelite by name Achan saw, coveted, took what
he was not meant to take, and troubled the camp. What one man did in secret affected the whole nation in battle. This
shows that God’s army is spiritually connected. The sin of one person can trouble a household, weaken a marriage, pollute
a family, damage a fellowship, hinder a local church, or affect a group assignment. This is not to create fear, suspicion, or
condemnation, but to teach us that private compromise is never as private as we think.

Ephesians gives the New Testament clarity for this lesson. Paul reminds us that “we are members one of another,” meaning
that the Church is one body and the actions of one member can affect others. He warns against lying, stealing, corrupt
communication, bitterness, wrath, anger, evil speaking, uncleanness, covetousness, and fellowship with darkness. These
are not small matters before God. They grieve the Holy Spirit, give place to the devil, and weaken the atmosphere of holiness
required for spiritual victory. Therefore, this study calls every TACEFite to take secret sin seriously. Besetting sins, cheating,
financial dishonesty, bitterness, gossip, covetousness, sexual compromise, and hidden uncleanness can weaken local revival
fire.

Teachings
1. One Man’s Sin Can Trouble the Camp Because the Body Is Spiritually Connected: The Bible begins Joshua 7 with a
striking statement: “But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing: for Achan... took of the accursed
thing.” Although Achan was the person who took the forbidden items, the Bible says the children of Israel committed a
trespass. This reveals the principle of corporate defilement. Achan sinned privately and alone, but the effect was felt
publicly. One man’s secret act brought defeat, shame, and grief upon the whole camp.

 ~ 125 ~

This may be difficult for some people to accept because we often think of sin only as a personal matter. We say, “It is my
life,” “It is my secret,” “It does not concern anybody,” or “Nobody is affected.” But the Word of God teaches that no member
of God’s people lives in complete isolation. In a family, one person’s action can affect the peace of the household. In a
marriage, one person’s secret sin can destroy the future of the children. In a fellowship, one person’s hidden compromise
can weaken the spiritual atmosphere. In a campus fellowship, one person’s moral failure can damage the credibility of the
whole work. In a church, the carelessness of a few can bring shame to many.

Ephesians 4:25 says, “Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour: for we are members one of
another.” This means that our purity, discipline, forgiveness, and obedience matter because we belong to one body. A
member of the body cannot wound himself without affecting the rest of the body. A hidden wound in one part can bring
pain to the whole body. In the same way, hidden sin in one life can trouble a group, family, fellowship, or church. This does
not mean we should become suspicious of one another or live in accusation. It means we must become more responsible
before God. We must understand that our secret lives matter. Our purity matters. Our honesty matters. Our handling of
money matters. Our relationships matter. Our hidden choices matter. The army of the Lord must not be weakened from
within by the secret compromise of those who are meant to be firebrands of revival.

2. Hidden Compromise Brings Defeat: Israel had just seen Jericho fall by the power of God. They had experienced victory
through divine strategy, obedience, and faith. Yet, soon after that victory, they were defeated by Ai, a smaller city. The issue
was not the size of Ai, but the state of Israel. A hidden sin had weakened the army. God said, “Therefore the children of
Israel could not stand before their enemies.” This means that hidden compromise can remove spiritual strength and make
God’s people vulnerable before battles they should have won.
This is a major warning to every revival army. We cannot win outward battles while tolerating inward pollution. We cannot
pray for revival while secretly living in sin. We cannot preach holiness while hiding impurity. We cannot confront darkness
while giving place to the devil in our private lives. Ephesians 4:27 says, “Neither give place to the devil.” Sin gives the enemy
space to operate. Bitterness, lies, stealing, corrupt communication, and unforgiveness give him space.
This is why ministry labour with impurity is rejected by God. The Lord is not only interested in what we do for Him but He
is interested in the state of the vessels doing the work. A singer can sing powerfully and still grieve the Holy Spirit. A preacher
can speak strongly and still be weakened by secret sin. A fellowship worker can be active and still be spiritually leaking. A
leader can organise programmes and still carry hidden immorality and bitterness. God does not separate the work from the
worker. The condition of the vessel affects the purity of the service.
Dear TACEFites, local revival fire can be weakened by sins we refuse to confront. Bitterness can poison fellowship. Cheating
can corrupt testimony. Financial dishonesty can destroy credibility. Sexual compromise can destroy the testimony of the
vision of revival. If we want to stand before the enemies of the Lord, we must remove the accursed thing from the camp.
3. Covetousness and Hidden Desires Can Destroy Victory: Achan’s confession shows the progression of sin. He said, “When
I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold... then I coveted
them, and took them.” First, he saw. Then he coveted. Then he took. Then he hid. This is how many secret sins grow. They
begin with unguarded sight, then unsurrendered desire, then sinful action, then hiding.

Covetousness made him value a garment, silver, and gold above the commandment of the Lord, the safety of the camp,
and the purpose of God. He wanted what God had forbidden, and he was willing to hide it under his tent.

Ephesians 5:3 warns that “fornication, and all uncleanness, or covetousness” should not be once named among saints.
Verse 5 further states that a “covetous man... is an idolater.” This means covetousness is not just wanting more but it is
allowing uncontrolled desire to become a god in one’s life. When desire controls a person, that person becomes capable of
lying, stealing, cheating, manipulating, betraying trust, or disobeying God. A person who is not content will cheat in
examinations, falsify records, steal funds, do online fraud called Yahoo-yahoo, exaggerate achievements, enter ungodly
relationships, misuse church resources, or compromise truth to gain advantage.

Dear TACEFites, our journey of victory can be destroyed by covetousness when our desires are no longer surrendered to
Christ. We must stop longing for what God has not given us, stop pretending to live a life we cannot afford, and stop entering
unnecessary debt just to impress people. Do not take loans from mobile apps to buy clothes, phones, shoes, wigs, gadgets,
or party outfits simply because you want to look successful before others. That path can lead to pressure, shame, lies,
anxiety, and deeper compromise. We must also reject the deception of “fake it till you make it.” A child of God is not called
to live by false appearance. Do not allow social media to push you into unhealthy comparison. Many pictures online do not

 ~ 126 ~

tell the full story. A person may change borrowed clothes several times just to take pictures for Instagram. Someone may
pose beside a car that does not belong to them. Do not let another person’s edited life make you despise your own process.
Always remember that godliness with contentment is great gain.
4. Sin Must Be Exposed and Judged through Repentance, Restitution, & Holiness: When Joshua lay before the Lord, God
told him to rise and deal with the sin in the camp. Prayer was important, but prayer was not a substitute for obedience.
God said, “Up, sanctify the people,” and also, “thou canst not stand before thine enemies, until ye take away the accursed
thing from among you.” This shows that hidden sin must not be covered, excused, or spiritualised. It must be exposed and
judged before the Lord. Achan eventually confessed, “Indeed I have sinned against the LORD God of Israel.” Confession is
necessary, but true repentance must go beyond words. The hidden items were brought out and laid before the Lord. This
teaches that sin must be brought into the light. Ephesians 5:11 says, “And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of
darkness, but rather reprove them.” Darkness survives by secrecy. Sin grows when it is hidden. Compromise becomes
stronger when it is protected. But when the light of God’s Word enters, darkness loses its hiding place.

True repentance produces fruits. It may require confession to God, apology to people, restitution where wrong has been
done under proper guidance and divine leading, accountability to mature believers, breaking ungodly relationships with
boyfriends and girlfriends, returning what was taken, correcting dishonest records, stopping corrupt communication, and
submitting to discipline. He that covers his sin will not prosper, but the one who confesses and forsakes sin will find mercy.
We must not only feel sorry because sin was exposed; we must turn away from it because it grieves God. Dear TACEFites,
secret sin must be treated seriously. The Lord is calling us to clean tents, truthful lips, pure hearts, honest hands, forgiving
spirits, disciplined desires, and lives that walk as children of light. If God wins our lives, He can use our lives to win others.

Step-by-Step Applications and Practical Implications
 • Search your tent before God: Set aside time this week to ask the Lord to search your heart, finances, relationships,
 words, habits, and secret life. Do not excuse what God is asking you to remove.
 • Treat private sin as a serious matter: Do not say, “It is only my secret.” Your life is connected to your spouse, family,
 fellowship, local church, workplace, and the body of Christ.
 • Remove every accursed thing: Identify any behaviour, object, relationship, habit, or hidden practice that is
 weakening your walk with God. Take clear steps to remove it.
 • Address covetousness and discontentment: Ask God to deliver you from unhealthy comparison, greed, pressure to
 belong, and desire for what He has forbidden.
 • Practise truthfulness: Put away lying, exaggeration, deception, dishonest claims, and false appearances. Speak the
 truth because we are members one of another.
 • Seek accountability: If you are struggling with a besetting sin, speak to a mature and trusted spiritual leader who
 can pray with you, guide you, and help you walk in victory.
 • Make restitution where necessary: Return what was taken, correct what was falsely presented, apologise where
 you wounded others, and repair what you damaged as the Lord leads and with the guidance of a spiritual leader

effect on others? Are there lies, dishonest dealings, secret habits, bitterness, gossip, covetousness, uncleanness, or wrong

Introduction
Our study this week takes us back to Ai, the same place where Israel had earlier suffered a painful defeat because of sin in
the camp due to the sin of one man called Achan. After the victory at Jericho, Israel assumed that Ai would be easy, but
they soon discovered that yesterday’s victory does not automatically guarantee today’s victory when hidden sin is
permitted and divine instruction is neglected. The first defeat at Ai exposed the danger of disobedience, self-confidence,
and unjudged sin. Yet, Joshua 8 shows us the depth of the mercy of God in restoring His army after failure. After sin had
been judged and obedience was renewed, the Lord spoke again to Joshua: “Fear not, neither be thou dismayed: take all the
people of war with thee, and arise, go up to Ai.” God did not abandon His army because they had failed; He restored them,
instructed them, and sent them again to win where they once lost.

The story of Ai teaches us that failure must not be hidden, excused, defended, or spiritualised. Grace restores, but grace
does not excuse sin. Sin must be dealt with honestly before God, and where necessary, before the people, so that holy fear,
caution, and spiritual seriousness can be restored in the great house. Yet correction must never become destruction. The
goal of godly correction is restoration, not rejection or dejection. The Lord’s army must learn how to stand again after
correction. None should be lost to sin. No backslider should be abandoned to the devil. No fallen soldier should be written
off when there is genuine repentance. After failure, confession, genuine repentance, renewed obedience, and fresh
instruction can bring the people of God back into victory.

Ephesians explains this restoration through the riches of God’s mercy and grace. Paul says, “But God, who is rich in mercy,”
and reminds us that even when we were dead in sins, God quickened us together with Christ. This means that the mercy
of God does not merely forgive; it raises. It does not only pardon; it restores. It does not only rescue us from the past; it

grace brings us back so that we can walk again in obedience, holiness, service, and divine purpose.

Teachings
1. God Can Restore a Defeated Army When Sin Is Judged and Obedience Is Renewed: Ai first appeared in Israel’s journey
as a place of shame, defeat, and painful correction. Israel had just seen the walls of Jericho fall by the power of God, but
they soon failed at Ai because sin had entered the camp. Yet Joshua 8 opens with a word of mercy: “Fear not, neither be
thou dismayed.” God was not finished with Joshua. God was not finished with Israel. The place of defeat was about to
become the place of renewed victory.

This is a major truth for every believer and every revival army. Failure is serious, but failure is not final when there is genuine
repentance. Sin must be judged, but the sinner who repents must be restored. A soldier may fall, but the Lord can raise him
again. A fellowship may make mistakes, but God can restore order. A believer may have failed in holiness, relationships, or
service, but mercy can bring such a person back to God. The devil wants failure to become permanent shame, but God
wants correction to lead to restoration. However, restoration does not happen by pretending nothing happened. God did
not restore Israel while sin remained hidden. Sin had to be exposed and judged before the army could rise again. Grace is
not a covering for sin but the power of God that brings us back into obedience.

2. Failure Must Be Confessed, Not Hidden, Excused, or Spiritualised: The defeat at Ai teaches that failure must be brought
into the light. When sin is hidden, it weakens the whole camp. When wrong is excused, the fear of God is reduced. When
failure is spiritualised, people avoid repentance and intentional change. Genuine restoration begins when a person stops
defending sin and begins to agree with God. There are many ways believers hide failure. Some blame others. Some say, “It
is my weakness”.Some excuse sin because of pressure, loneliness, disappointment, family background, or past wounds.
Some use spiritual activities to cover secret sins. Some continue to serve publicly while refusing to deal with private sin.
Others become silent and withdraw because they feel ashamed, but they do not open up for help, correction, and
restoration.

The path of restoration is confession, repentance, correction, cleansing, and renewed obedience. This connects with
repentance as a daily posture for the believer as we learned last year. Repentance is not only for the day we first came to
Christ. A believer must keep a tender conscience before God. When the Holy Spirit convicts us, we must not delay. When
the Word exposes us, we must not argue. When godly leaders correct us, we must not harden our hearts.
There is also a place for open rebuke when sin is public, damaging, or capable of weakening others. This is not for
humiliation or cruelty, but to restore holy fear, protect the flock, and preserve order in the great house. Open rebuke must
be done with wisdom, love, and spiritual maturity. The goal is not to disgrace people, but to prevent sin from becoming
normal. The church must not make repentance difficult for those who have fallen or make sin comfortable for those who
refuse to repent

3. Victory Cannot Rest on Yesterday’s Method: When Israel first went against Ai, they approached the battle with
confidence drawn from the recent victory at Jericho. They assumed that Ai would be easy. But after correction and
repentance, God did not simply tell Joshua to repeat the Jericho method. He gave a fresh instruction for Ai. Jericho fell
through marching, trumpet, silence, and shout. Ai was taken through a different strategy involving careful positioning,
ambush, timing, and renewed obedience. This teaches that every spiritual advance requires specific new leading from God.
What God used before must not become a formula we now apply without seeking Him. A method that worked in one
season may not be the instruction for another season. We must always ask, “Lord, what are You saying now?”

Presumption is dangerous because it assumes God will support what we have not submitted to Him. Israel could not defeat
Ai by mere courage. They needed renewed instructions. In the same way, TACEFites must not enter academic decisions,
career choices, ministry efforts, relationships, financial decisions, mission work, or fellowship plans based only on past
experience. We need fresh leading. God told Joshua, “Arise, go up to Ai,” but He also gave a specific strategy. Restoration
does not mean rushing back carelessly into activity. After failure, there must be humility to patiently wait and ask for
direction again. The restored soldier must not return with pride, but with obedience. The army that will win after failure
must listen again, obey again, and move again under the fresh command of the Lord.

4. Restoration Requires the Renewal of the Word and Grace for Good Works: After the victory at Ai, Joshua did something
very important. He built an altar unto the Lord, wrote a copy of the law of Moses upon stones, and read all the words of

the law before the congregation. This means that victory after failure had to be followed by the renewal of covenant with
God. Israel must not only win a battle but must also return to the Word. They must remember the blessings and warnings
of the covenant. They must hear again what God had commanded. The Word had to be brought back to the centre.

After failure and restoration, we must not only feel relieved that God has forgiven us. We must return to the Word. We
must read it, meditate on it, obey it, and live it. The Word restores order to the heart, renews conviction, rebuilds spiritual
discipline and teaches us how to walk carefully after mercy has restored us. Ephesians 6:13 says, “having done all, to stand.”
After failure, stand. After correction, stand. After repentance, stand. After restoration, stand. After renewed instruction,
stand. The devil may accuse but stand. Shame may speak but stand. People may remember your failure but stand in humility
and renewed obedience. God’s mercy can make the place of defeat become the place of testimony.

Step-by-Step Applications and Practical Implications
• Do not hide failure: If you have fallen into sin, prayerlessness, bitterness, dishonesty, or immorality, bring it honestly
 before God.
• Seek godly help quickly: Do not withdraw into shame. Speak to a mature discipler, fellowship leader, or trusted spiritual
 guide who can help you return to God properly.
• Receive correction with humility: Correction is not rejection. God corrects those He wants to restore. Do not resist
 rebuke.
• Restore holiness before service: Do not rush back into activity without dealing with the root of the fall. Rebuild your
 altar, Word life, prayer life, relationships, and walk with God.
• Ask God for fresh instruction: Do not assume that yesterday’s method will win today’s battle. Ask the Lord for present
 leading in your life, ministry, business, marriage, academics, career, family, and fellowship.
• Return to the Word: Read, meditate on, obey, and live the Word. Let Scripture renew your mind, restore order, rebuild
 conviction, and guide your next steps.
• Help fallen soldiers return: Do not mock, gossip, or abandon those who have failed. Pray for them, restore them in
 meekness.
• Stand again: After genuine repentance and restoration, do not give up. Arise again, serve again, pray again, fight again,
 and win in the strength of the Lord.

SECTION 4: How God’s Army Must Return to the Word, Discern Deception, Stand against United Opposition, and Give
No Place to the Devil

The journey of God’s end-time army does not end with the first victories of possession; it now enters a deeper season of
discernment, covenant order, and enlarged warfare. After Jericho had fallen and Ai had been conquered, Joshua brought
the people back to the altar and to the public reading of the Word. This teaches us that victory must not carry God’s people
away from God. Every conquest must return to worship, every breakthrough must deepen obedience, and every movement
of revival must remain rooted in the Word. The army that will continue to possess the land must not only know how to
fight; it must know how to hear, read, obey, and live by the Word of God.

After victory, the enemy does not always return with open warfare; sometimes he comes through deception, false peace,
attractive offers, and ungodly alliances. The Gibeonites did not come with swords; they came with old bread, worn

 ~ 134 ~

garments, and a convincing story. This teaches that not every harmless-looking offer is from God. Not every peaceful
proposal is spiritually safe. Not every good-looking partnership, relationship, business opportunity, ministry collaboration,
or life decision carries divine approval. God’s army must therefore walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise.
Discernment, prayer, patience, and spiritual counsel are necessary to preserve inheritance.

Ephesians explains this section by calling us back to the Word, wisdom, spiritual alertness, and warfare. The Word of God
is the sword of the Spirit, and it must shape the whole army. Ephesians also warns us to walk circumspectly, redeem the
time, and avoid deception. As opposition multiplies, we are commanded to be strong in the Lord and in the power of His
might, because we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against organised spiritual forces that resist God’s purpose.
Therefore, TACEFites must understand that expanded inheritance will often attract expanded warfare.

This fourth section therefore calls the Lord’s army to become Word-rooted, discerning, prayerful, and spiritually alert. We
must not allow victory to become carelessness. We must not make covenant decisions by appearance alone. We must not
fear when enemies join forces against the work of God. We must not leave hidden kings and unfinished battles to grow
again in secret. The army that will possess the land must keep returning to the Word, test every alliance, stand firm when
opposition multiplies, and give no place to the devil.

Week 16: Mount Ebal and the Altar of the Word - Returning Victory to Covenant Obedience: After victory at Ai, Joshua
built an altar and read all the words of the law before the people. This teaches that conquest must return to worship and
covenant obedience. The whole army, men, women, children, leaders, and strangers, needed the Word. We must remain
deeply rooted in the Scripture, sound doctrine, meditation, and daily obedience. Revival must not become an activity
without the Word, emotion without doctrine, or conquest without covenant.

Week 17: The Gibeonite Deception - The Need for Discernment, Prayer, and the Danger of Unholy Alliances: The
Gibeonites teach us that deception often appears harmless, reasonable, peaceful, and attractive to natural judgement. Old
bread can hide false identity. Because Israel did not ask counsel of the Lord, they entered into a covenant that created long-
term crisis and pain. TACEFites must not make marital, career, business, investment, ministry, or partnership decisions by
appearance only.

Week 18: When Enemies Come Together - Standing Firm When Opposition Multiplies: As Israel’s possession expanded,
enemies began to unite against them. This teaches that the mandate of winning souls and possessing territories for Christ
will attract resistance. Darkness does not easily give up territories it has occupied. Yet, no coalition of enemies can cancel
divine purpose when God’s people stand in submission, alignment, and prayer. TACEFites must not fear multiplied
resistance. Spiritual warfare intensifies as inheritance expands, but one with God is a majority.

Week 19: The Hidden Kings and Unfinished Battles - Giving No Place to the Devil: Joshua’s pursuit of the hidden kings
teaches that victory must be completed and not left unfinished. Hidden enemies, tolerated compromises, secret sins,
unresolved bitterness, careless habits, and unjudged patterns can rise again if they are not dealt with. Ephesians warns us
to give no place to the devil. TACEFites must therefore close every spiritual opening, confront hidden battles, and refuse to
allow small compromises to become future strongholds. The Lord’s army must finish well, stand firm, and leave no room
for the enemy to regain ground.

Title: Mount Ebal and the Altar of the Word: Returning Victory to Covenant Obedience

Bible Texts: Joshua 8:30-35; Ephesians 5:15-17; Ephesians 6:17

Introduction
As we start this new section of study this week, we are brought into a very important moment after the victory at Ai. Joshua
did not allow the success of battle to become a reason for spiritual carelessness. After Israel had risen again from failure,
received fresh instructions, and won where they once lost, Joshua led the people to Mount Ebal and built an altar unto the
Lord God of Israel. He offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. He wrote a copy of the law of Moses on stones and read
all the words of the law before the whole congregation. This teaches us that victory must always return us back to intimate
fellowship with the Lord. The Lord’s great and exceeding army must never become so excited about success that it forgets
the God who gave the victory.

Mount Ebal teaches that possession must remain under continued fellowship and covenant obedience. The people had
won a battle, but they still needed the Word. They had conquered a city, but they still needed to hear the law of God. They
had seen divine restoration after failure, but they still needed to be gathered around the altar and the Scriptures. Men,
women, children, leaders, officers, judges, elders, strangers, and those born among them all stood and learn before the
Word. Joshua read everything. There was not a word of all that Moses commanded which he did not read. This means that
the whole army must be shaped by the whole counsel of God. Victory must not take God’s people away from the Word; it
must drive them deeper into fellowship and covenant consciousness.

Ephesians deepens this lesson by showing that the people of God must walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise,
understanding what the will of the Lord is. The will of God cannot be properly understood outside the Word of God. A
revival army that moves without Scripture will soon become emotional, careless, and easily corrupted. Ephesians also calls
the Word of God “the sword of the Spirit.” This means the Word is not only for teaching; it is also a weapon for warfare,
discernment, correction, defence, and victory. Therefore, TACEFites must keep the Word as an integral core in the execution
of the mandate of revival. We must raise a generation that is worded, deeply rooted in Scripture, vast in doctrine, and

careful to meditate on the Word until it becomes practical obedience in everyday living. Revival must not become activity
without the Word and every victory must bring us back to the altar, back to Scripture, back to obedience, and back to
deeper encounter with the Lord.

Teachings
1. Every Victory Must Lead to Intimate Fellowship: After the victory at Ai, Joshua built an altar unto the Lord God of Israel
in Mount Ebal. Joshua did not rush from one victory to another without stopping to worship, fellowship and reconnect with
his source. He did not allow the excitement of victory and busy ministerial schedule to replace personal fellowship and
reverence for God. He understood that victory belongs to the Lord, and every victory must return to the Lord in deeper
intimacy, thanksgiving, surrender, and renewed obedience.

This is a major lesson for the Lord’s army because the danger after victory is that the heart can become careless. A student
may succeed academically and forget the God who gave wisdom. A worker may receive promotion or secure a new job and
become too busy for fellowship or even quiet time. A mother may receive the gift of a baby and use the baby as an excuse
for being too busy to serve the Lord. This is why every increase, victory and enlargement must end at God’s altar. The altar
reminds us that every victory came from Him and must be returned to Him.

Joshua’s altar was not built according to personal preference. It was built “as it is written in the book of the law of Moses.”
This means worship, fellowship and intimacy with God must also be governed by the Word. True worship is not emotional
singing, loud sound, or religious activity but a life returned to God in obedience and a heart of thanksgiving that leads to
surrender. Dear TACEFites, every answer to prayer must take us closer to God. Every breakthrough must increase our loyalty
to the Lord. Every career, financial and life opportunity must increase our obedience. Every lifting must bring us back to the
altar. If victory takes us away from our relationship with God, then we are already in danger. The Lord’s army must learn to
win and still worship, possess and still bow, advance and still remain broken before God.

2. The Whole Army Must Be Shaped by the Whole Word: Joshua wrote a copy of the law of Moses on stones and read all
the words of the law before the people. The Scripture says, “There was not a word of all that Moses commanded, which
Joshua read not.” This shows us that God’s revival army must not be shaped by partial truth, selected verses, popular
quotable quotes, or emotional messages alone. The whole army needs the whole Word. The Word was read to all Israel,
including elders, officers, judges, women, little ones, strangers, and those born among them. The Word was not reserved
only for leaders, teachers, ministers, or older believers. Everyone needed the Word, including the children. Do not let us
turn our Sunday school children’s classes to cartoon playground without the Word of the Lord being taught. The whole
congregation need to hear, understand, and be shaped by the commandment of the Lord.

As we pursue the mandate of revival, we must not raise a generation that is active but shallow, excited but not grounded,
gifted but not governed, or zealous but not doctrinally sound. We must raise TACEFites who are worded, deeply rooted in
Scripture, trained in doctrine, and able to apply the Word to everyday life. The Word must shape our homes, studies,
careers, relationships, dressing, speech, leadership, fellowship, evangelism, finances, service, and private conduct. If the
Word does not shape us, social media will shape us. If the Word does not govern us, culture will govern us. If doctrine does
not settle us, emotion will move us. Therefore, the Word must be read, taught, meditated upon, obeyed, and lived by all.

3. Revival without the Word Becomes Dangerous, Shallow, and Easily Corrupted: Israel had begun to possess the land,
but Joshua brought them back to the Word. This teaches that every revival movement, spiritual activity, or ministry advance
becomes dangerous when it is not grounded in the Word of God. Today, we organise many programmes described as revival,
but they often focus more on what participants can receive from God in the short term than on what God who to make of
their lives in the long term. The emphasis is commonly on blessings, riches, healing, miracles, promotion, breakthroughs,
open doors, and material enlargement. These things are not wrong, but Jesus called them “all these things” that should
follow those who first seek the kingdom of God and His righteousness. True revival must go beyond what God can give us
to what God can remove from us, correct in us, and produce through us. It must lead to repentance, holiness, obedience,
humility, love, spiritual discipline, and conformity to the character of Christ. When the Word is absent, programmes can
produce excitement without transformation. We see people receive prophecies without knowing Jesus, celebrate miracles
without overcoming sin, and speak loudly about spiritual experiences while remaining weak in spiritual substance. This is
why Ephesians says, “See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise.” The Word helps us walk carefully. It
checks our motives, corrects our excesses, exposes our errors, strengthens our convictions, and guides our decisions.

Without the Word, a revival movement can be sincere but sincerely wrong. We can be active for God without being aligned
with God, and loud in spiritual language while lacking the nature of Christ.

Revival without Scripture also becomes easily corrupted because popularity, growth, testimonies, and visible success attract
pride, imitation, manipulation, and compromise. A fellowship that grows numerically may reduce the demands of
discipleship in order to retain the crowd. A ministry that becomes popular may entertain rather than teach, while a gifted
leader may depend on manifestations and neglect the secret place. Beloved, the absence of Scripture is a doorway to
spiritual decay. Any spiritual labour that lacks the Word may appear impressive for a season, but it will eventually become
worthless. Jesus taught that the seed without sufficient depth sprang up quickly but withered when pressure came. In the
same way, revival that produces excitement without roots cannot raise believers who endure temptation, persecution,
disappointment, or delay. The true evidence of revival is not what happens during the programme but what remains after
the meeting ends. Are people more prayerful, holy, loving, truthful, disciplined, and obedient? Are they grounded in sound
doctrine? Are they becoming disciples who can disciple others?

4. The Word Is the Sword of the Spirit for Wisdom, Warfare, and Daily Obedience:
Ephesians 6:17 calls the Word of God “the sword of the Spirit.” This means that the Word is not only a book to read but a
weapon to carry. It is the Spirit’s sword in the hands, mouth, mind, and heart of the believer. No army can fight well without
a sword. No TACEFite can stand well without the Word. No revival work can remain pure without Scripture. The sword of
the Spirit helps us fight lies, temptations, fear, unbelief, deception, false doctrine, compromise, spiritual confusion, and
every thought that opposes the will of God. When Jesus was tempted in the wilderness, He answered with the Word of
God. In the same way, every believer must learn to answer the enemy, the flesh, the world, and wrong thoughts with the
Scripture. The Word of God must be in our hearts through meditation, in our mouths through confession, in our decisions
through obedience, and in our lives through practice.

Ephesians 5:17 also says, “Wherefore be ye not unwise, but understanding what the will of the Lord is.” The Word of God
helps us understand the will of the Lord at all times. Many believers are confused because they want directions outside the
Scripture. They want spiritual power without scriptural guidelines. They want victory without obedience. But the Word
reveals God’s mind, trains our discernment, and helps us know what pleases the Lord. For us in the great house of TACEF,
this means that the Word must remain at the centre of the revival mandate. We must not only be prayerful; we must be
scriptural. We must not only be zealous; we must be doctrinally sound. Beloved, read the Word, study the Word, memorise
the Word, meditate on the Word, obey the Word and most importantly live the Word. The army that is deeply rooted in
the Word of God will not be deceived, corrupted, or defeated.

5. Step-by-Step Applications and Practical Implications
• Return every victory to God: After every answer to prayer, breakthrough, success, promotion, deliverance, or ministry
 impact, deliberately return to God in intimate fellowship, thanksgiving, and renewed surrender.
• Build a personal altar of the Word: Set a daily time to read, meditate on, and respond to Scripture. Do not only read
 the Bible for the purposes of preaching or fellowship assignments.
• Read the Word to all: Parents should read and explain Scripture to children. Leaders should teach younger believers.
 Fellowship leaders must ensure new converts and members are grounded in the Word.
• Become worded: Commit to becoming deeply rooted in the Scripture and sound doctrine. Do not be a believer who
 only knows songs and quotable quotes but cannot explain basic truth from the Word.
• Apply the Word daily: Apply the Lord’s instruction from Scripture each day and obey it practically in your speech,
 dressing, relationships, studies, work, finances, and private life.
• Use the Word as a sword: When temptation, fear, discouragement, anger, lust, pride, or unbelief comes, answer with
 the Word of God, not with feelings.
• Walk circumspectly: Before making decisions, ask, “What does the Word of God say? Is this wise? Does this reflect the
 will of the Lord?”

Introduction
We progress our study this week as God’s exceeding great army into the critical matter of the deception of the Gibeonites,
one of the most important lessons on discernment in the journey of winning the hearts of men and our generation for the
Lord. After Jericho had fallen and Ai had been conquered, the enemies of Israel began to respond in different ways. Some
kings gathered themselves together to fight with Joshua and Israel. But the inhabitants of Gibeon chose another method.
They did not come openly with weapons; they came with deception. They took old bags, old wine bottles, old shoes, old
garments, and dry, mouldy bread, pretending that they had come from a far country. Their appearance looked harmless,
their request sounded peaceful, and their words seemed reasonable. Yet behind the old bread and worn garments was a
false identity.

The tragedy of this story is not only that the Gibeonites deceived Israel, but that Israel made a covenant with them without
asking counsel at the mouth of the Lord. The Bible says, “And the men … asked not counsel at the mouth of the LORD.”
Joshua and the princes examined the evidence before them, listened to their story, considered the old bread, and made
peace with them. After three days, they discovered that the people were not from a far country, but their neighbours who
dwelt among them. This teaches us that human judgement is not enough for the Lord’s army. What looks peaceful may not
be safe. What sounds respectful may not be sincere. Every revival army must learn that we do not live by sight, and we
must not be ruled by appearances.

Ephesians deepens this lesson by warning believers against deception, vain words, unfruitful works of darkness, and
ungodly alliances or association. Paul says, “Let no man deceive you with vain words,” and then commands, “See then that
ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise.” To walk circumspectly is to walk carefully, prayerfully, watchfully, and with
spiritual understanding. Ephesians also teaches us to prove what is acceptable unto the Lord. This means that every
relationship, partnership, offer, opportunity, ministry collaboration, career direction, business proposal, investment
decision, and life milestone must be tested by the Word, prayer, spiritual counsel, and the leading of the Holy Spirit. This
study calls all TACEFites to learn the practice of discernment in all decisions. Not every open door is God’s door and not
every opportunity carries divine approval. Covenant decisions require time to seek the Lord, and all life milestones must
not be handled in haste.

Teachings
1. Deception Often Appears Harmless, Peaceful, and Reasonable: The Gibeonites did not approach Israel with open
violence. They did not come as obvious enemies. They came as humble travellers who came from a very far country, seeking
peace. Their presentation was carefully arranged to convince Israel. Their old sacks, torn bottles, worn shoes, old garments,
and mouldy bread were all part of the deception. Everything they showed Israel was designed to make their story
believable. This teaches us that deception does not always appear evil at first. Sometimes deception appears harmless and
peaceful. Sometimes it sounds respectful, religious, sympathetic, and reasonable. The Gibeonites even spoke about the
name of the Lord and what He had done in Egypt and beyond Jordan. They used spiritual language, but their intention was
false. This means that speaking like a believer and using spiritual language alone is not proof of spiritual truth. A person,
proposal, relationship, opportunity, or partnership can sound spiritual to us and still be dangerous. Many believers have
entered marriage only to discover that the calm, tongue-speaking brother they married was merely wearing a Christian
mask, while his true character told a very different story. Likewise, some have married sisters who appeared godly, humble,
and submissive during courtship, only to discover later that it was pretence all the way.

Natural judgement can easily be impressed by what it sees and hears. Israel looked at the bread and the garments. They
listened to the story and everything appeared to agree, but appearance was not truth. This is why the Lord’s revival army

 ~ 142 ~

must not be ruled by impressions, pity, pressure, or packaging. We must not assume that every calm voice is truthful, every
humble posture is sincere, every spiritual statement is God-led, or every partnership offer is from God. Dear TACEFites, in
these last days, discernment is critical. Deception will not always announce itself as deception. It may come as a friendly
social media request, an invitation to a so-called professional club by a respected brother in church, a well-packaged
partnership offer at a Christian event, a juicy job or scholarship opportunity, an exciting investment proposal, or even an
invitation to minister in song from someone you deeply admire. Beloved, we must not be careless, even as we remain kind
and loving. We must be open-hearted, but not spiritually blind. We must walk in wisdom, because not everything that
appears harmless is safe.

2. Do not Be Ruled by Appearances: The Gibeonites used old bread to support a false identity. They said the bread had
been taken hot from their houses when they began the journey but had become dry and mouldy because they had travelled
from a very far country. The bread became their evidence. The old garments became their proof. The worn shoes became
their argument. Yet everything was arranged to support a lie. This is a serious warning because what people present as
evidence may not always reveal the truth. A person can package a story to create sympathy and generate pity. A proposal
can be arranged to look urgent. A relationship can be presented as harmless. A business opportunity can be dressed as
destiny helper has come. A ministry collaboration can be wrapped in religious language while an offer for a career relocation
may be well packaged to deceive us of our hard-earned money. Beloved, be aware that appearance can be manipulated,
but truth must be discerned.

This is the essential reason why we are told to “walk by faith, not by sight.” We must not live by sight, because sight can be
deceived and manipulated. Sight sees the bread, but the Spirit searches the matter. Sight sees the garment, but the Word
tests the fruit. Sight hears the story, but prayer brings the matter before God. When we depend only on what is seen, we
may make decisions that create long-term crisis and problems with no end. Beloved, please see beyond the packaging. In
marriage decisions, we must not be deceived by beauty, so-called spiritual gifts, education, or family background. In career
decisions, we must not choose because of immediate gains, salary, title, or prestige. In ministry and church decisions, we
must not choose by popularity, crowd, or invitation. We must ask: What is the spirit behind this? Is this consistent with the
Word? Is there peace in the Holy Ghost? Have I prayed? Have I sought godly counsel? Is this helping or weakening my walk
with God?
3. Human Judgement Is Not Enough: The men of Israel actually suspected something at first. They asked, “How do we know
you aren’t local people? How could we then make a covenant with you? (Message version)” This means there was already
a warning sign. Something in the matter required deeper enquiry. Yet, instead of taking the matter to the Lord, they
continued the conversation and later made a covenant. This is the reality of many of us. We sometimes have a quiet
suspicion, an inward hesitation, or a small unrest in the spirit, but we ignore it because the opportunity looks too good, the
people sound sincere, or the evidence appears convincing. Many times, the Lord in His mercy prompts us to check a matter
again before we commit ourselves. It may come through the quiet voice of a wife saying to her husband, “Dear, can we pray
more about this?” It may come through a child saying, “Mummy, I am not sure we should invest this money.” It may come
through a spiritual son or daughter saying, “I do not think we should invite that minister to our fellowship.” Sometimes,
God uses these simple cautions as divine interruptions to slow us down before we enter a covenant, partnership,
relationship, investment, or decision that may later bring trouble. Therefore, we must not despise godly caution. The Lord
can use a spouse, a child, a junior person, a spiritual mentee, or even a quiet burden in our heart to call us back to prayer.

Moreover, our text of study this week gives the root of the mistake clearly: “And asked not counsel at the mouth of the
LORD.” This is the central lesson of the Gibeonite’s deception. Israel did not fail because there was no evidence but because
they trusted evidence without enquiry from God. They did not fail because they were unintelligent; they failed because
intelligence cannot replace divine guidance. They did not fail because they were weak soldiers; they failed because strong
soldiers can still make wrong decisions when they neglect prayer.

4. Prayerlessness Opens the Door to Error and Long-Term Problems: Joshua made peace with the Gibeonites, and the
princes of the congregation swore unto them. After three days, the truth was revealed. The Gibeonites were not from a far
country; they were neighbours dwelling among them. But because Israel had sworn by the Lord God of Israel, they could
no longer simply destroy them. This teaches that rash and hasty decisions can create long-term consequences. Some
decisions are not easily reversed. Many erroneous commitments, relationships, vows, agreements, partnerships, business
commitments, ministry connections, financial obligations, and marital choices can create troubles that continue for years.
This is why we must never be in haste to make decisions on life milestones. The fact that an offer is urgent does not mean

 ~ 143 ~

it is divine. The fact that a door is open does not mean God opened it. The fact that people are pressuring you does not
mean you must act immediately.

We must also understand that lack of prayer in decision making opens the door to error because it leaves the soul under
the rule of appearance, emotion, fear, greed, and human persuasion. When prayer is absent, the flesh becomes louder.
When the Word is not consulted, worldly reasoning becomes normal. Ephesians warns us not to be partakers with darkness,
but to walk as children of light. This requires carefulness, separation, and patience to wait when we appear to be too slow
and the courage to say no when everyone is putting us under pressure. Beloved, do not make marital, career, business,
investment, ministry, relocation, leadership, or partnership decisions by appearance. Seek God’s accurate leading. Pray,
wait, test the matter by the Word, seek mature counsel. Do not be rushed because perfect discernment protects
inheritance.

5. Step-by-Step Applications and Practical Implications
 • Do not be ruled by appearance: Do not make decisions by what looks good, sounds peaceful, appears urgent, or
 seems profitable.
 • Ask counsel at the mouth of the Lord: Before entering major decisions, take the matter to God in prayer and wait
 for His guidance.
 • Test every offer by the Word: Ask whether the decision agrees with Scripture, strengthens holiness, preserves
 peace, and honours Christ.
 • Watch spiritual language carefully: Do not assume that a person, group, proposal, or opportunity is safe because
 it uses spiritual words or appears “Christian-like”
 • Slow down covenant decisions: Marriage, business, investment, ministry partnerships, relocation, and career
 choices require prayer, patience, counsel, and discernment.
 • Seek godly counsel: Speak with spiritually mature leaders, disciplers, and trusted believers before major
 commitments.
 • Pay attention to warning signs: When there is inner unrest, inconsistency, pressure, or confusion, do not ignore it.
 • Walk as a child of light: Refuse unfruitful works of darkness, ungodly alliances, and relationships that weaken your
 walk with God.

Title: When Enemies Come Together: Standing Firm When Opposition Multiplies

Bible Texts: Joshua 10:1-15; Ephesians 6:10-13

of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil. 12 For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against

Key Extracts from the Bible Texts to Remember and Reflect On
 • The five kings of the Amorites gathered themselves together.
 • All the kings of the Amorites that dwell in the mountains are gathered together against us.
 • Fear them not: for I have delivered them into thine hand.
 • There shall not a man of them stand before thee.
 • The LORD discomfited them before Israel.

Introduction
Our study this week explored the moment when the enemies of Israel began to unite together to fight against the progress
of God’s people. After Jericho had fallen, Ai had been conquered, and Gibeon had made peace with Israel, Adonizedek,
king of Jerusalem at that time, became afraid. He saw that the influence of Israel was spreading and that territories were
beginning to fall as the army of the Lord advanced. It is important to note that the Gibeonites who deceived Israel into an

 ~ 146 ~

alliance were not from a small place, but from a great city, one of the royal cities, and all its men were mighty. So, when the
whole city of Gibeon aligned with Israel, the surrounding kings recognised that the force of Israel was not ordinary and that
the balance of power in the land had changed. Therefore, five kings gathered themselves together to fight against Gibeon
because it had made peace with the children of Israel.

This study teaches us that the mandate of winning souls for the Lord as an exceeding great army will attract oppositions.
Darkness does not quietly surrender territories it has occupied. When souls begin to turn to the Lord, when campuses begin
to open to revival, when local churches begin to awake unto righteousness, when families begin to return to holiness, when
young people begin to stand for truth, and when communities begin to experience the light of Christ, opposition will arise.
Sometimes the enemy fights as one force; at other times, enemies come together in networks and alliances with intense
pressures, accusations, distractions, temptations, discouragements, and organised resistance. Yet, we know that no
coalition of darkness can cancel divine purpose when God’s people stand in obedience and submission.

The book of Ephesians deepens this lesson by showing that spiritual warfare is real. Paul tells us to be strong in the Lord
and in the power of His might, and to put on the whole armour of God because we wrestle not against flesh and blood. He
then describes four layers of organised spiritual oppositions: principalities, powers, rulers of the darkness of this world, and
spiritual wickedness in high places, which we have also studied in Week 12. These speak of demonic structures, authorities,
forces, and operations that resist the advancement of God’s purpose in lives, families, churches, communities, and
territories. The battle is never against people but against the unseen forces that use systems, cultures, fears, bondages, and
spiritual blindness to resist the rule of Christ. As we advance as a revival army to win our territories and hearts of men for
the Lord, we must expect resistance because spiritual warfare intensifies as inheritance expands. The enemy may form
stronger networks to scatter focus, corrupt purity, frustrate leadership, discourage intercession, or resist soul-winning, but
we must hold strong from the standpoint of victory in Christ.

Teachings
1. The Mandate of Winning Souls and Possessing the Land Attracts Opposition: The five kings did not gather together
simply because Israel existed. They gathered because Israel was advancing in its destiny to take over the Promised Land.
They saw clearly that Jericho had fallen, Ai had been conquered, and Gibeon had made peace with Israel. The influence of
God’s people was spreading, and the kings of the land became afraid. The enemy’s response is often to oppose the
expansion of God’s work, and this opposition increases when territory begins to shift. We know that the mandate of winning
souls for the Lord will always attract resistance because every soul saved is a territory reclaimed from darkness, every home
restored to holiness is a territory recovered for Christ, and every campus touched by revival is a territory challenged by the
Kingdom of God. In the same vein, every local church awakened unto repentance is a territory where darkness begins to
lose ground, and every workplace where a believer stands for righteousness becomes a place where Christ’s light confronts
corruption, and spiritual darkness. This is why the enemy resists soul-winning, discipleship, holiness, and revival.

Darkness is not only interested in individual sin but seeks territorial influence as it works through cultures, patterns, ungodly
systems, false beliefs, addictions, fear, pride, lust, and spiritual blindness to keep lives and communities under bondage.
Territorial domination means that darkness tries to normalise sin, silence truth, weaken prayer, corrupt leadership, and
make people comfortable without God. Therefore, as God’s exceeding great army of revival, we must not be surprised
when resistance rises as the mandate advances. When you begin to win souls, distractions may multiply. When a local
fellowship begins to grow, opposition may arise through church politics and even through other groups/societies within the
church. Do not be moved. Please learn to focus on drawing strength and power from the Lord through sustained
intercession and spiritual warfare. Do not shift your attention to men or the crisis itself. Continue to stand in warfare until
the strongholds controlling the hearts of men and initiating the tensions are broken, because everything we see in the
physical answers to spiritual powers behind the scenes. We must also note that the increase of opposition does not mean
God is absent. It only means that the territory is being contested. Therefore, we stand firm, because the Lord who called us
also fights with us.

2. Enemies Can Unite against God’s End-Time Agenda, but No Coalition Can Cancel Divine Purpose: King Adonizedek did
not fight alone. He sent to other kings, saying, “Come up unto me, and help me.” The five kings gathered themselves
together with all their hosts and made war against Gibeon. This was a coalition battle. Their strength was multiplied, their
armies were gathered, and their intention was clear. They wanted to punish Gibeon for aligning with the God of Israel and
stop the spread of Israel’s influence. This is a clear picture of how opposition can network against God’s end-time agenda.
Sometimes different forces that do not normally agree can suddenly unite against revival, salvation message and the

 ~ 147 ~

advancement of God’s Kingdom. In our instance, we may see a collation of false doctrine, discouragement, family pressure,
financial pressure, health challenges, distraction, confusion, relationship battles, institutional resistance, and spiritual
attacks appearing together to overwhelm us, weaken our hands and get us from our duty posts.

Ephesians 6:12 helps us understand this more deeply. Paul says we wrestle against principalities, powers, rulers of the
darkness of this world, and spiritual wickedness in high places. These are organised spiritual forces of evil and demonic
hierarchies that resist believers as they advance the purpose of God. Jesus also revealed that demonic powers can operate
in organised networks, as seen in the “Legion” of demons in Mark 5:9. He further taught that victory over a territory requires
first binding the “strong man” who exercises influence over it, as seen in Matthew 12:29. He also warned that evil spirits
can return to a life with additional forces to strengthen their hold if their influence is not permanently displaced (Matthew
12:43-45). This shows that spiritual warfare is not casual but involves confronting organised forces of darkness through the
authority of Christ in warfare prayer.

3. Fear Must Not Control the Revival Army When Resistance Multiplies: When Gibeon came under attack, the men of
Gibeon cried to Joshua, saying, “Slack not thy hand from thy servants; come up to us quickly, and save us, and help us.” The
situation was urgent. All the kings of the Amorites that dwelt in the mountains had gathered against them. Naturally, this
could have produced fear. But the Lord spoke to Joshua, saying, “Fear them not: for I have delivered them into thine hand;
there shall not a man of them stand before thee.”

This word from the Lord is very important. God did not deny that the enemies had gathered or that there was no opposition,
but instead, He gave Joshua a higher truth: “Fear them not.” Fear must not be the controlling spirit of the revival army.
When fear controls the heart, obedience becomes weak and when fear rules the mind, prayer becomes unstable. As revival
army, we must know that when fear enters our camp, we begin to see the enemy more than the promise of God.

The sovereignty of God must settle the heart of every soldier. God rules over our lives, our battles, our assignments, our
seasons, and our enemies. No darkness can overrule His purpose. If He sends us, He will sustain us. If He commands us, He
will back us. If He promises victory, no enemy can stand before Him. However, this sense of assurance does not mean we
should be careless. Joshua still acted. He moved all night. He took the people of war and the mighty men of valour because
faith does not remove responsibility. However, Joshua moved without fear because the Lord had spoken and he acted from
confidence in God, not panic before the enemy.

4. God Fights with His People And His Power over Nature: Joshua responded to the cry of Gibeon and went up from Gilgal
with all the people of war and all the mighty men of valour. The Lord had spoken, and Joshua obeyed. Then the Bible says,
“And the LORD discomfited them before Israel.” The word “discomfited” means that God threw the enemy into confusion,
panic, disorder, and terror. The enemies plans broke down, their coordination failed, their confidence melted away, and
they became unable to fight effectively. What Israel could not have achieved by military strength, the Lord accomplished,
by supernaturally troubling the enemy camp and turning their strengths into weakness before His people. This is the secret
of divine victory when we allow the Lord to fight for us as we follow His leading.

The battle at Gibeon also teaches that God enlists creation for His redemptive agenda. As the Lord cast down great stones
from heaven, Joshua spoke, commanding the sun to stand still over Gibeon and the moon over the valley of Ajalon. Nature
submitted perfectly to fulfill God’s purpose, proving that the Creator of all things can command all things, influencing
weather, solar systems, timing, seasons, and resources for His glory. Remarkably, this event aligns with modern science. A
2017 study by Cambridge University researchers re-examined the original Hebrew text, revealing that the phrase translated
as "stand still" (dôm) can linguistically mean "to stop shining." By recalculating ancient planetary orbits, scientists confirmed
that a rare annular solar eclipse passed directly over Canaan on October 30, 1207 BCE, providing a concrete, scientifically
verifiable anchor for the biblical timeline.

5. Step-by-Step Applications and Practical Implications
• Expect resistance: Do not be surprised when opposition rises as you pursue soul-winning, discipleship, holiness, prayer,
 and revival.
• Discern territorial battles: Recognise that some challenges are not merely personal, but connected to souls, families,
 campuses, local churches, workplaces, and communities being reclaimed for Christ.
• Do not fight people as enemies: Remember that we wrestle not against flesh and blood. Love people, but confront the
 spiritual forces behind bondage and resistance through prayer.

 ~ 148 ~

• Put on the whole armour of God: Stand in truth, righteousness, faith, salvation, the Word of God, and prayer. Do not
 face battles with carelessness or compromise.
• Practise corporate intercession: Organise prayer burdens around families, local churches, campuses, workplaces,
 communities, cities, nations and unsaved souls.
• Stand from victory, not fear: Pray knowing that Christ has already conquered. Warfare prayer is not panic but it is
 enforcing victory through faith on what Christ has done already.
• Remain aligned with God: Check your motives, methods, obedience, holiness, and submission. God fights with those
 who stand in His will.
• Trust God for unusual help: Believe that God can command circumstances, timing, opportunities, resources, and even
 creation to serve His redemptive purpose.

that God can command nature, circumstances, timing, resources, and creation for His redemptive purpose and for our
good?
