Introduction
At this point in Israel’s journey, Joshua died. He had served the purpose of God in his generation. He had followed Moses,
carried the burden of leadership, led Israel across Jordan, fought the battles of possession, divided the inheritance, warned
the people, renewed covenant commitment, and finished his course. Scripture honoured him as “the servant of the LORD.”
Yet, his death taught a very serious lesson that leaders would finish their course, but the purpose of God must not die with
them.

Joshua’s life had great influence. Israel served the Lord all the days of’ Joshua and all the days of the elders that outlived
him, those who had known the works of the Lord. But Judges later recorded one of the saddest statements in Scripture:
“There arose another generation after them, which knew not the LORD, nor yet the works which he had done for Israel.”
This means that a generation can enjoy revival, witness miracles, inherit testimonies, and still fail to raise another
generation that knows the Lord personally. When the realities of God are not deliberately transferred, a people can move
from revival legacy to spiritual ignorance.

This is a major warning to the house of TACEF. The revival mandate must not die with one generation of leaders, executives,
ministers, or intercessors. God’s work is bigger than one person, one leader, one fellowship, one family, or one generation.

 ~ 265 ~

If the next generation only hears stories of past revival and moves of God without personal encounter, deep discipleship,
and spiritual responsibility, they may inherit structures without fire. They may inherit songs with no burden. They may
inherit activities with no encounter.

Ephesians gives us the pattern for continuity. Christ is the Head of the Church, and He gives ministry gifts for the perfecting
of the saints, for the work of the ministry, and for the edifying of the body. This means leaders are not given to gather
dependants around themselves forever. They are given to equip saints until the body matures and every part supplies its
measure. A healthy revival movement is not personality-dependent but it is Christ-centred, Word-rooted, Spirit-
empowered, and disciple-making. Therefore, this week calls TACEFites into radical discipleship. Every local fellowship must
become a training ground. Everyone associated with the vision of revival must be taught, mentored, assigned, supervised,
corrected, encouraged, and released into responsible service. Every leader must ask, “Who am I raising? Who will carry
this burden after me? Who is learning the way of the Lord through my life?” True revival is preserved when disciples
become disciple-makers.

Teachings
1. Leaders Finish Their Course, but God’s Movement Must Not Die with Them: Joshua died after serving God faithfully.
This is a sobering truth because no matter how anointed, gifted, committed, or beloved a leader may be, every human
vessel has a season. Moses died. Joshua died. The elders died. Leaders may change, executives may rotate, ministers may
be transferred, campus leaders may graduate, brethren may relocate, and parents may grow old, but the purpose of God
must continue. This is why no revival movement should depend only on one person or group of persons. When a work
depends entirely on one leader’s charisma, presence, energy, sacrifice, or authority, the work becomes weak and fragile.
If that person travels, relocates, changes role, or dies, the movement may suffer because the burden was not properly
transferred. God’s work is too precious to be held only in one hand.

Joshua was a great leader, but Israel still needed continuity beyond Joshua. The people served the Lord during his lifetime
and during the lifetime of the elders who had seen the works of God. This shows the power of godly leadership and living
witnesses. When those who know God are present, they can preserve truth, correct error, inspire faith, and remind the
people of God’s dealings. But if those witnesses do not raise others who also know the Lord, the next generation may
become spiritually empty. The great house of TACEF must therefore refuse personality-dependent revival. We must
definitely honour fathers, mothers, leaders, and pioneers, but we must not build the work around human personality.
Christ is the Head. The vision belongs to the Lord. Leaders are vessels, not owners. They are stewards, not substitutes for
Christ. When leaders are celebrated more than Christ, the next generation may inherit admiration without conviction.

2. The Tragedy of a Generation That Knows Not the Lord: Judges says, “There arose another generation after them, which
knew not the LORD, nor yet the works which he had done for Israel.” This is one of the saddest outcomes after a season of
great divine visitation. A people who crossed Jordan, saw Jericho fall, experienced victories, and entered inheritance still
produced a later generation that did not know the Lord. The problem was not that the earlier generation had no
testimonies but the problem was that those testimonies did not become personal knowledge of God in the next generation.
There is a difference between hearing about God and knowing God like we studied in our last spiritual year. A child may
hear that God answered the prayers of his parents, but still not know the Lord personally. A young TACEFite may hear
stories of past conventions, revivals, missions, and sacrifices, but still not have an encounter with Christ. A new member
may enjoy fellowship activities, but still not be grounded in salvation, holiness, prayer, and the Word. A young person may
inherit a Christian family name, but not inherit the fear of God.

This is the danger of revival move without discipleship. The next generation may know our songs but not our tears. They
may know our programmes but not our burden. They may know our fellowship vision as quotable quotes but not our
covenant. They may know our leaders but not our Lord. They may know our testimonies but not the God who gave them.
When this happens, a movement can remain busy while spiritual reality fades. Apostle Paul understood this danger. He
told Timothy to commit the truth to faithful men who would be able to teach others also. This is the principle of
generational transfer. Paul taught Timothy. Timothy was to teach faithful men. Those faithful men were to teach others
also. Truth must not stop with the person who received it. The failure to raise a generation that knows the Lord can happen
in homes, churches, fellowships, and ministries. Parents can be active in church while their children are spiritually
neglected. Leaders can organise programmes while young members remain undiscipled. Ministers can preach to crowds
but fail to raise faithful workers. Fellowship executives can run activities but leave no successors. Therefore, we must

 ~ 266 ~

intentionally bring the next generation into salvation, encounter, holiness, and most importantly, a personal knowledge of
Christ.

3. Discipleship Preserves Continuity by Intentionally Raising Successors: Discipleship is the deliberate process of helping
people know Christ, grow in Christ, become like Christ, serve Christ, and reproduce the life of Christ in others. It is more
than teaching a class. It is more than inviting someone to a programme. It is more than giving someone a role. Discipleship
is formation which shapes belief, character, habits, choices, service, doctrine, discipline, and burden. Jesus did not only
preach to crowds, He made disciples. He called them, stayed with them, taught them, corrected them, sent them, rebuked
them, explained truth to them, modelled prayer before them, and entrusted responsibility to them. Discipleship therefore
requires nearness, patience, truth, love, example, correction, repetition, and responsibility. It is a very intentional labour.

The principles of discipleship are very practical. First, discipleship begins with salvation. People must know the Lord
personally. We must not assume that everyone attending fellowship is born again. Second, discipleship grounds people in
the Word of God. A disciple must know what Scripture teaches, not only what popular culture says. Third, discipleship
builds spiritual disciplines: prayer, study, fasting, fellowship, obedience, evangelism, giving, and service. Fourth,
discipleship shapes character, that is, humility, truthfulness, purity, patience, faithfulness, teachability, and love. Fifth,
discipleship involves correction. A disciple who cannot be corrected cannot be properly formed. Correction must be done
with love, but it must not be avoided. Sixth, discipleship involves assignment. People grow by doing. A new believer can
learn to pray, follow up, serve, teach children, support outreach, and help others under supervision. Seventh, discipleship
involves accountability. Someone must ask, “How are you growing? How is your prayer life? Are you walking in holiness?
What are you learning?” Eighth, discipleship involves reproduction. A disciple must eventually help disciple others.

4. The Heart and Lifestyle of a Discipler Must Be Worth Following: A discipler is not only someone who teaches; a discipler
is someone whose life helps others follow Christ. Paul said, “Be ye followers of me, even as I also am of Christ.” This is the
heart of true discipleship. The discipler does not draw people to himself or herself. The discipler says, “Follow me only as I
follow Christ.” The life of the discipler must point to Christ, not replace Christ. The heart of a discipler must be filled with
love because discipleship is not control, manipulation, or the desire to gather followers around oneself. It is spiritual
parenting that carries burden, patience, sacrifice, and compassion. A discipler must love people enough to teach them,
correct them, forgive them, encourage them, and continue with them as they grow. Disciples do not mature in one day.
Some will be slow. Some will make mistakes. Some will need repeated teaching. The discipler must carry the heart of Christ.

The lifestyle of a discipler must also be credible. People should be able to observe the discipler’s prayer life, humility, purity,
faithfulness, service, speech, family life, stewardship, and response to correction. A discipler who teaches holiness but lives
carelessly will weaken disciples. A discipler who teaches humility but is proud will confuse followers. A discipler who
teaches service but avoids sacrifice will raise careless workers. Life is a better curriculum than words. This does not mean
a discipler must be perfect but he or she must be sincere, teachable, repentant, accountable, and growing. When a discipler
makes a mistake, he or she must be humble enough to acknowledge it. When corrected, the discipler must not become
defensive. Disciples learn not only from our victories but also from how we handle weaknesses with humility and truth.
The discipler must also avoid making disciples dependent on his or her personality. The goal is to connect people to Christ.
True disciplers raise people who can hear God, obey the Word, serve faithfully, submit, and disciple others. They are not
threatened when others grow. They rejoice when disciples become fruitful.

5. Step-by-Step Applications and Practical Implications
 · Do not let the work die with you: Share burdens, document processes, train others, and raise successors before
 transition comes.
 · Avoid personality-dependent revival: Honour leaders, but keep Christ as the Head and centre of the work.
 · Raise the next generation intentionally: Children, teenagers, youths, new members, and young workers must be
 taught, mentored, corrected, and released into service.
 · Do not assume people know the Lord: Teach salvation, assurance, holiness, prayer, the Word, fellowship, and
 personal encounter with Christ.
 · Create service pipelines: Welcome new members, identify gifts, assign mentors, give small responsibilities,
 supervise, and release gradually.
 · Practise full discipleship: Disciple belief, character, prayer life, service, stewardship, and relationships.
 · Use correction as formation: Correct with love, patience, clarity, and truth. Do not avoid correction because it is
 uncomfortable.

 ~ 267 ~

· Let disciples grow by doing: Give people opportunities to serve under supervision instead of waiting until they
 appear perfect.
 · Disciple at home: Parents and guardians must raise children who know the Lord personally, not only children who
 attend church.
 · Live a followable life: Let your lifestyle, speech, humility, holiness, marriage, service, sacrifice, and accountability
 point people to Christ.
 · Raise disciple-makers: Do not only gather people around yourself. Train them to disciple others.

myself? What must change in my life so that I can become a faithful discipler?

Title: The Bones of Joseph: The Resurrection of the Dead and End-Time Truths

Bible Texts: Joshua 24:32; Genesis 50:24-26; Hebrews 11:22; Ephesians 1:9-11

Bible Texts
Joshua 24:32: 32 And the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, buried they in Shechem, in
a parcel of ground which Jacob bought of the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for an hundred pieces of silver: and it

Key Extracts from the Bible Texts to Remember and Reflect On
 • The bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt.
 • God will surely visit you.
 • Ye shall carry up my bones from hence.
 • By faith Joseph, when he died…gave commandment concerning his bones.
 • Having made known unto us the mystery of his will.
 • According to his good pleasure which he hath purposed in himself.
 • In the dispensation of the fulness of times.
 • He might gather together in one all things in Christ.

Introduction
Our 52-week Bible study this week brings us to a short but deeply prophetic verse in Joshua 24: “And the bones of Joseph,
which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, buried they in Shechem.” On the surface, this may look like a simple
burial record, but it carries a deep spiritual meaning and application to us as God’s end-time army. Joseph died in Egypt,
but before his death, he made a request concerning his bones. He said, “God will surely visit you,” and commanded that
when God brought Israel out of Egypt, they should carry his bones with them. Hebrews later tells us that this instruction
was an act of faith: “By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Israel; and gave
commandment concerning his bones.” Joseph lived in Egypt with honour, influence, wealth, status, and royal access, but
he knew Egypt was not his final home. He had seen greatness in Egypt, but his heart remained tied to the promise God
gave Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. His bones became his final testimony that God would keep His covenant. He could not
physically walk out of Egypt with Israel, but his bones would travel with them. His coffin became a silent witness that Egypt
was not the end of the story and that death could not cancel the promise of God.

This is why Joseph’s bones are more than a family burial matter. They teach us about faith beyond death, covenant hope,
resurrection expectation, and end-time readiness. Every time Israel carried Joseph’s bones through the wilderness, they
were carrying a testimony that God’s promises outlive human’s breath. Joseph was saying, “Do not leave me in Egypt,
because God will surely visit you.” His bones were a physical prophecy that the grave is not the believer’s final location.
Death is not the end. The body may be buried, but the story of the redeemed is not finished. There is a resurrection of the
dead, and the saints shall rise.

 ~ 270 ~

Ephesians tells us that God has made known unto us the mystery of His will, and that in the fullness of times He will gather
together in one all things in Christ, both in heaven and on earth. This means God has an eternal plan. The exodus, the
wilderness journey, the burial of Joseph’s bones, the resurrection of Christ, the hope of the saints, the rapture, the second
coming, the millennial reign, final judgement, and the new heavens and new earth all sit within God’s sovereign purpose.
He works all things after the counsel of His own will. Therefore, this week calls every TACEFite to live like Joseph: faithful
in Egypt, but not owned by Egypt; useful in the present world, but not trapped by the present world; blessed here, but
prepared for the eternal inheritance. We must live with resurrection hope. We must understand the end-time truths of
Scripture. We must prepare for the coming of the Lord. We must not make this world our final home.

Teachings
1. Joseph’s Bones Were a Declaration That Egypt Was Not His Final Home: Joseph died in Egypt, but he refused to let
Egypt define his final resting place. He had risen to a place of great influence in Egypt. He was second in command to King
Pharaoh. Yet, at the end of his life, his heart was still in the promise of God. He said, “God will surely visit you, and bring
you out of this land.” This statement showed that Joseph’s faith was not swallowed by his success. This is a strong lesson
for TACEFites. God can lift a believer in “Egypt” that is, in the systems, structures, nations, careers, institutions, and
platforms of this present world, but the believer must not forget our true identity that we are citizens of heaven on a short
pilgrimage on earth. Joseph served excellently in Egypt, but he did not become an Egyptian in covenant identity. He worked
in Egypt, but his hope was not in Egypt. He succeeded in Egypt, but his future remained tied to the covenant of God.

This is an important area where many believers struggle. When God blesses them with education, promotion, relocation,
influence, wealth, business growth, public honour, or ministry lifting, they begin to settle in this present world as if it is
their final home. They forget that we are pilgrims. They begin to live as if comfort, status, and earthly success are the final
definition of life. But Joseph’s attitude teaches us to enjoy God’s blessing, serve faithfully where He places you, but do not
forget your eternal home. Joseph’s instruction concerning his bones was his vote of absolute confidence in the promise of
God. He believed that God would surely visit Israel. He believed the exodus would happen, even though he would not live
to see it in the flesh. He believed that his body belonged in the land of promise, not in Egypt. This was faith beyond his
lifetime. It was faith that looked past death, past delay, past slavery, past wilderness, and into the fulfillment of God’s
word.

2. Joseph’s Bones Preach the Resurrection of the Dead: Joseph’s bones travelling through the wilderness served as a
lesson to Israel. For many years, the children of Israel carried the remains of a man through the wilderness for forty long
years. Every time they saw that coffin, they were reminded that God’s covenant was stronger than death. Joseph was dead,
but his faith was still speaking. His bones were saying, “God will surely visit you.” His bones were saying, “Egypt is not our
final resting place.” His bones were saying, “Death does not have the final word.” This points us to the truth of resurrection.
The believer does not see death the way the world sees death. Death is real and painful, but for the redeemed, it is not
final defeat. The body may be laid in the ground, but God has not finished with the body. Scripture teaches that the dead
in Christ shall rise. The same Lord who raised Jesus from the dead will also raise the saints. The grave is not the final home
of the believer but a temporary waiting place until the voice of the Son of God calls the dead to rise.

Joseph’s burial in Shechem also teaches that the body matters. The Christian hope is not only that the soul goes to be with
the Lord; it also includes the resurrection of the body. God created the body, redeemed the believer, and will raise the
body in glory. This is why the resurrection of Christ is central to our faith. If Christ is risen, then those who sleep in Him
shall also rise. The resurrection of Jesus is the firstfruits and the guarantee of the believer’s resurrection.
This truth should comfort the Church because loved ones who die in Christ are not lost forever and the saints who slept in
the Lord are not forgotten. Their bodies may return to the dust, but the Lord knows His own. At the sound of the trumpet,
the dead in Christ shall rise first, and living believers shall be caught up together with them to meet the Lord in the air. This
is our blessed hope and therefore we must not fear death like those who have no hope. It also means we must not live
anyhow. If there is resurrection, then holiness matters. If there is resurrection, then every TACEFite must live ready for the
coming of the Lord.

3. God’s Eternal Plan Will Gather All Things in Christ: Ephesians 1:10 says that in the dispensation of the fullness of times,
God will gather together in one all things in Christ, both which are in heaven and which are on earth. This is one of the
deepest statements about the end of all things because all history is moving towards Christ. The promises to Israel, the
resurrection of the saints, the judgement of evil, the renewal of creation, and the eternal inheritance of the redeemed all
find their fulfillment in Him. While Joseph’s bones were buried in Shechem, in the land of promise, the burial was not the

 ~ 271 ~

end of the story. The land itself points to inheritance, the inheritance points to covenant, and covenant points to Christ.
Christ is the One in whom all the promises of God find their fulfillment. He is the risen Lord, the Head of the Church, the
coming King, and the One in whom all things will be gathered. This gives every believer confidence that God does not
abandon His promises.

This also gives meaning to our labour. When we preach the gospel, we are participating in God’s eternal plan to gather
people into Christ. When we live holy, we are declaring that this world is not our final home. When we bury a saint in hope,
we are saying that resurrection is coming. When we endure suffering for Christ, we are saying that eternal glory is greater
than present pain. Every TACEF revival army must therefore be an eternity-conscious army. Our fellowships, homes,
ministries, missions, prayer meetings, evangelism, and discipleship must be shaped by the coming of the Lord. We must
therefore raise Christians who only want earthly blessings but have no burden for heaven.

4. The Seven Major Events of the Last Days: This section revisits the major end-time truths we studied in our last spiritual
year as a reminder of the same burden of living like Joseph, knowing that this present world is not our final home. These
truths are not given to frighten us, but to awaken holiness, readiness, and eternal perspective.
 • The Rapture - The Sudden Gathering of the Saints: The rapture is the sudden catching away of the saints to meet
 the Lord. Scripture says, “For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout... and the dead in Christ shall
 rise first.” Then living believers shall be caught up together with them to meet the Lord in the air. The rapture will
 happen like a thief coming in the night.
 • The Marriage Supper of the Lamb - The Celebration of the Redeemed: The Marriage Supper of the Lamb is the
 heavenly celebration of Christ and His redeemed Church who were taken up during Rapture. It reminds us that
 holiness, faithfulness, and endurance are not in vain. The Bride must make herself ready. Every labour, sacrifice,
 purity, service, and obedience done for Christ will be remembered.
 • The Tribulation - A Period of Great Sorrow and Judgement: The tribulation will be a time of great distress,
 deception, and judgement upon the earth after true believers have been raptured. Scripture speaks of great
 trouble, false worship, global control, and severe pressure on those left behind. We should not study this with
 curiosity only, but with holy seriousness. If such judgement is coming upon a Christ-rejecting world, then we must
 preach the gospel urgently and live ready for the Lord.
 • The Second Coming of Christ -The Triumphant Return of the King: The second coming is the visible, glorious return
 of Christ to the earth. Unlike the rapture, where believers are caught up to meet the Lord, the second coming
 reveals Christ openly as King and Judge. He will defeat evil, judge the nations, and establish His righteous reign.
 • The Millennial Reign of Christ - Christ’s One Thousand-Year Reign on Earth: After His return, Christ will reign on
 earth in righteousness. Satan will be bound, and the earth will experience divine government, justice, peace, and
 restoration. Faithful saints will reign with Him. This teaches us that present faithfulness prepares us for future
 responsibility.
 • The Final Judgement -Eternal Separation of the Righteous and the Wicked: The final judgement reveals the
 seriousness of eternity. Those whose names are not found in the book of life will face eternal judgement. This is
 not a subject for careless argument but a call to repentance, evangelism, holiness, and compassion for the lost.
 Every believer must never be casual about souls. Hell is real, judgement is real, and salvation in Christ is the only
 hope.
 • The New Heavens and the New Earth -The Eternal Dwelling of the Saints: The new heavens and the new earth are
 the final dwelling of the redeemed. God will dwell with His people. Sin, death, sorrow, pain, and tears will be gone
 forever. This is the believer’s eternal home. Joseph knew Egypt was not his home, and we must also know that

Title: The Priesthood of Eleazar: Standing As A Revival Priest Across Generations

Bible Texts: Joshua 24:33; Exodus 19:5-6; Numbers 16:46-48; Ephesians 2:19-22; Ephesians 4:1-6

Bible Texts
Joshua 24:33: 33 And Eleazar the son of Aaron died; and they buried him in a hill that pertained to Phinehas his son, which
was given him in mount Ephraim.

Exodus 19:5-6: 5 Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure
unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine: 6 And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation.
These are the words which thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel.

Numbers 16:46-48: 46 And Moses said unto Aaron, Take a censer, and put fire therein from off the altar, and put on incense,
and go quickly unto the congregation, and make an atonement for them: for there is wrath gone out from the LORD; the
plague is begun. 47 And Aaron took as Moses commanded, and ran into the midst of the congregation; and, behold, the
plague was begun among the people: and he put on incense, and made an atonement for the people. 48 And he stood
between the dead and the living; and the plague was stayed.

Ephesians 2:19-22: 19 Now, therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of
the household of God; 20 And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the
chief corner stone; 21 In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord: 22 In whom
ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit.

Key Extracts from the Bible Texts to Remember and Reflect On
 • Eleazar the son of Aaron died.
 • Ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests.
 • And an holy nation.
 • He stood between the dead and the living.
 • The plague was stayed.
 • Fellowcitizens with the saints.
 • Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone.
 • Groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord.
 • An habitation of God through the Spirit.

Introduction
This week brings us to the burial of Eleazar, the son of Aaron. Joshua had died, Joseph’s bones had been buried in Shechem,
and now Eleazar, the high priest also died and was buried in the portion connected to Phinehas his son. This short record
is not only a note about the end of a priest’s life but a sober reminder that priesthood, intercession, and covenant
responsibility must be preserved across generations. Joshua represented leadership in battle and inheritance. Eleazar
represented priestly continuity, altar order, divine enquiry, covenant mediation, and the preservation of worship before
the Lord. Eleazar’s life reminds us that every move of God needs priests who will keep the altar fire burning. Revival move
requires intercessors, burden-bearers, watchmen, consecrated servants, and men and women who understand how to
stand before God on behalf of the people. However, we must also understand the larger purpose of God on how priests
should function. While Eleazar belonged to the Aaronic priesthood, God’s original plan for Israel was far broader because
He said, “Ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation.” God wanted an entire people, and not one tribe
(Levi) out of twelves tribes, who could walk in covenant access, holiness, and priestly nearness before Him.

Israel’s fear at Sinai and later idolatry revealed the weakness of the people, and the priestly responsibility became
structurally preserved through the tribe of Levi and the house of Aaron. Men like Aaron, Eleazar, and Phinehas became
central to sustaining the altar, guarding the sanctuary, and bearing the burdens of the nation before God. Yet, the original
plan remained that God desired a holy people who would live near Him.

 ~ 275 ~

This is important for all TACEFites. We must not outsource intimacy with God to ministers, leaders, or executives. Every
believer must have a priestly identity. Every home must have priestly responsibility. Every local fellowship must become
an altar of spiritual priests. Every TACEFite must know how to pray, stand in the gap, carry burdens, and connect heaven.
Therefore, this week calls us to become a priestly revival army who must stand between the living and the dead through
intercession. We must wear the spiritual garments of burden-bearing by carrying people on our shoulders and in our hearts
before God. True revival is sustained when every believer understands the call to be a priest before God.

Teachings
1. From Eleazar to a Kingdom of Priests: Eleazar was the son of Aaron, the brother of Moses who was the first high priest
in Israel. After Aaron died, Eleazar continued the work of the priesthood. In those days, priests had a very important role
in Israel. They offered sacrifices for the sins of the people, taught the Word of God, cared for the things of God, and stood
before God on behalf of the nation. They helped the people know how to worship God and remain in covenant with Him.
So, when the Bible records the burial of Eleazar, it reminds us that priestly service was a major part of Israel’s journey with
God, and it was as important as reporting the death of Joshua. The role of priest is to help the nation of Israel remain close
to God through the services at the altar. Without the altar, Israel would lose its spiritual centre. Without priests, the people
could easily forget God, drift into sin, and lose the fear of the Lord. But God’s original plan was even bigger than having
only a few priests where only one tribe will serve as priests out of the twelve tribes. In Exodus 19:6, God told Israel, “Ye
shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation.” This means God wanted the whole nation to know Him, walk
with Him, obey Him, and function as priests with direct access. He did not want only Aaron, Eleazar, and the tribe of Levi
to be close to Him while everyone else stayed far away. God wanted all His people to live near Him.

However, when Israel came to Mount Sinai, they were afraid at the glory of God. They stood far away and asked Moses to
speak with God on their behalf. Later, when they made the golden calf, it showed that their hearts were not fully ready to
live as a holy nation of priests. Because of this, God used the tribe of Levi and the family of Aaron to preserve the priestly
work. What was meant to be available to all Israelites was now limited to a tribe and priests like Eleazar to keep the altar,
sacrifices, worship, and teaching alive among His people. For us today, the lesson is clear. God does not want us to serve
Him from a distance. Through Jesus Christ, every believer can come near to God. We do not need to depend only on
ministers or leaders to pray, study the Word, hear God, or live holy. Every believer is called to know God personally and
represent God wherever he or she is.
This means every TACEFite must see himself or herself as part of God’s priestly people. We must not be distant followers
of God.

2. The Priest as a Revival Intercessor Standing Between the Living and the Dead: One of the most powerful pictures of
the role of a priest is the art of intercession as seen in Numbers 16. When judgement began to move through the
congregation, Moses told Aaron to take a censer, put fire from the altar in it, put on incense, and go quickly to the people.
Aaron did not stand far away analysing the crisis. He ran into the midst of the congregation with altar fire and incense.
Scripture says, “And he stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stayed.” This is the heart of a revival
intercessor. A priest does not watch spiritual decay with a critical spirit. A priest does not complain about a dying
generation, dead altar, shrinking congregation, worldly members, careless youths, broken homes, corrupt institutions,
failing churches, compromised leaders, or declining morality, but they run to the altar, take holy fire, carry incense, and
stand in the gap in true intercession because every priest uses prayers to trigger divine intervention.

“To stand between the living and the dead” means to pray for people who may not yet know how to pray for themselves.
It means to carry the burden of a family member drifting from God, intercede for children, teenagers, students, workers,
ministers, fathers, mothers, churches, and nations. It also means to cry for mercy over others. It means to resist spiritual
death through prayer, fasting, and tears. A revival intercessor must also act quickly. Moses said Aaron should “go quickly.”
The priestly army must discern urgency and respond quickly with prayer.

3. The Garments of the Priest - Carrying People on the Shoulders and in the Heart: The garments worn by high priest
further explain the work of priests as they represent spiritual symbols of burden-bearing. In Exodus 28, the high priest
carried the names of the tribes of Israel on onyx stones upon his shoulders and on precious stones in the breastplate over
his heart. This means the priest did not enter the holy place as an individual but as a carrier of a people. He carried their
names, their needs, their battles, their failures, and their hopes before God. The shoulder speaks of responsibility. To carry
names on the shoulders means to bear the weight of others before God. The priest must be strong enough in God to carry
burdens that are not convenient. This is what intercessors do. They carry families, fellowships, ministries, children, youths,

 ~ 276 ~

leaders, the sick, the weak, the confused, the backsliding, the broken, and the unreached before the Lord. They do not
drop the burden because it is heavy.

The breastplate over the heart speaks of love, affection, compassion, and intimate concern. The priest must not carry
people only as assignments but must carry them with love. It is possible to carry responsibility without affection. It is
possible to lead people without truly loving them. It is possible to pray mechanically without compassion. But priestly
intercession requires both shoulder and heart, that is, strength and love, responsibility and compassion. This is important
for every revival army in TACEF. We must carry people as priests. A fellowship coordinator must not only plan meetings
but must carry souls in prayer. A children’s teacher must not only teach lessons, but she must carry children before God in
continued prayers.

Priestly garments also teach sustained intercession. The priest did not wear the stones only once. They were part of his
priestly identity. In the same way, intercession is not something we do only during emergencies but a lifestyle. The burden
of people must not disappear after one prayer meeting. Names must be remembered, families must be mentioned before
God, struggling brethren must be carried, leaders must be prayed for, the weak must be strengthened, and the lost must
be sought. Dear TACEFites, wear the spiritual garments of priesthood and let your shoulder be available for responsibility
and your heart be alive with compassion.

4. Identificational Repentance - Carrying the Pain and Sin of the People Before God: True revival does not come through
detached, finger-pointing prayers. A priest does not stand above the people in pride, saying, “Look at what they have
done.” A priest kneels before God and says, “We have sinned.” This is the principle of identificational repentance. It means
standing before God as part of the people we represent, confessing corporate guilt, crying for mercy, and asking God to
heal what is broken. Daniel gives us a powerful example. He was personally faithful as an individual, yet when he prayed
for Israel, he did not say, “They have sinned.” He said, “We have sinned.” Nehemiah did the same. Ezra also identified with
the shame and failure of the people. These men did not excuse sin, but they did not pray with a proud distance from the
people either. They carried the pain, rebellion, blindness, and failure of the nation before God.
This is priestly prayer of a revival army where we ask for divine mercies over families, fellowships, parents, leaders,
believers, and even other watchmen. Identificational repentance does not mean taking personal guilt for sins one did not
commit in a legal sense but means coming before God as a representative burden-bearer. It means saying, “Lord, we are
part of this family, this fellowship, this Church, this nation, this generation, and we are asking for mercy.” This is a priestly
posture that carries the pain of the people into the presence of God.

TACEFites must learn this kind of prayer because identificational repentance creates compassion. When we pray this way,
we stop treating people as problems and begin to carry them as souls. We stop mocking the fallen and start seeking their
restoration. Dear TACEFites, the Lord is calling us to priestly repentance for our families, fellowships, churches, campuses,
communities, and nation. Let us confess, cry, intercede, and carry the burden until mercy speaks. A priestly army does not
only preach revival but travails for revival.

5. Step-by-Step Applications and Practical Implications
 · Recover priestly identity: Do not outsource intimacy with God to leaders, ministers, or intercessors. Every believer
 has access to God through Christ.
 · Keep the altar fire burning: Build consistent prayer, Bible study, and obedience in your personal life and home.
 · Stand in the gap: Do not only criticise spiritual decline. Pray, fast, counsel, teach, follow up, and carry burdens
 before God.
 · Respond quickly to spiritual danger: When a family, fellowship, marriage, or believer is drifting, do not delay in
 prayer and loving intercession.
 · Carry people on your shoulders: Accept responsibility for souls, families, fellowships, and communities God has
 placed in your care.
 · Carry people over your heart: Do not lead, teach, pray, or serve without compassion, love, and tenderness.
 · Use names in prayer: Mention people, families, converts, leaders, and communities specifically before God.
 · Practise sustained intercession: Do not pray once and forget. Continue until burdens lift, lives change, and mercy
 speaks.
 · Practise identificational repentance: Confess corporate failures before God with a burden for mercy, healing, and
 restoration.

Week 50: Monday, 9 August 2027 to Sunday, 15 August 2027
Title: Summaries from Joshua, Part 1: The Consecration of an Exceeding Great Army

Bible Texts: Joshua 3:5; Joshua 5:2-9; Joshua 7:10-13; Joshua 23:11-13; Ephesians 4:22-24; Ephesians 5:8-11; Ephesians
6:24

Key Extracts from the Bible Texts to Remember and Reflect On
 · Sanctify yourselves: for to morrow the LORD will do wonders among you.
 · This day have I rolled away the reproach of Egypt from off you.
 · They have also transgressed my covenant.
 · Thou canst not stand before thine enemies, until ye take away the accursed thing from among you.
 · Take good heed therefore unto yourselves.
 · They shall be snares and traps unto you.
 · Put off concerning the former conversation the old man.
 · Be renewed in the spirit of your mind.
 · Have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness.

Introduction
This week’s study begins the final cross-thematic summary of our journey through Joshua and Ephesians. For many weeks,
we have walked with Joshua from his making as a servant, minister, disciple, warrior, leader, and covenant witness. We
have seen Israel cross the Jordan, confront Jericho, fall at Ai, recover through repentance, return to the Word, discern
deception, possess inheritance, renew covenant, raise successors, remember resurrection hope, and recover priestly
burden. As we now gather the whole study into three closing themes, the first focus is to understand that an exceeding
great army must be a consecrated army.

The issue of consecration is the foundation of everything in a man’s walk with God. Before Jordan opened, Joshua said,
“Sanctify yourselves: for to morrow the LORD will do wonders among you.” Before Israel could fight major battles in the
land, God brought them to Gilgal where the reproach of Egypt was rolled away. Before Ai could be conquered after failure,
God exposed the accursed thing and demanded sanctification. Before Joshua left the stage, he warned Israel to take good
heed unto themselves and love the Lord their God. This means the army that will last must be an army that belongs wholly
to God. The book of Joshua teaches us that God does not merely gather people but prepares them. He does not only give
promises but requires obedience. He does not only open doors, but He also deals with the heart. He does not only bring
His people into inheritance, but He warns them against backsliding, strange gods, hidden sin, wrong attachments, and
careless living. An exceeding great army is not defined first by number, noise, title, history, visibility, or activity, but by their
holy separation unto God.

Ephesians gives the same New Testament clarity that we must put off the old man, be renewed in the spirit of our minds,
and put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness. We must walk as children of light.
We cannot be part of God’s revival army and still be comfortable with the unfruitful works of darkness. The life of Christ
must affect our hearts, speech, relationships, ambitions, and private choices. Therefore, Week 50 study calls all TACEFites
to review the entire study through the lens of consecration. We must ask: What old reproach must be rolled away? What
accursed thing must be judged in my life? What hidden compromise must be confessed and forsaken now? What wrong
attachment must be broken? What casual Christianity must be rejected? What love for God must be restored?

Teachings
1. Consecration Is the First Requirement of an Exceeding Great Army: When Israel stood before Jordan, Joshua did not
first tell them to sharpen swords, count soldiers, design strategies, or study the river. He said, “Sanctify yourselves.” This
teaches that the first preparation for divine wonders is not external arrangement but inward consecration. God was about
to do what human strength could not do, but the people had to be prepared before Him. The Lord who opens rivers also
requires clean vessels. This principle has appeared again and again throughout our study. Before God uses a people as an
army, He makes them and making starts by being set apart alone for the Lord. Consecration means being separated unto
God. It means that the life is no longer available for every appetite, influence, relationship, habit, ambition, and pleasure.
It means that God has total claim over the body, heart, time, money, thoughts, speech, gifts, home, work, and future. A

 ~ 281 ~

consecrated believer does not ask, “Is this convenient?” He asks, “Does this please the Lord?” He does not ask, “Can I do
it?” He asks, “Will this preserve my walk with God?”.

As heaven-conscious revival army, we must understand that consecration is practical. It affects what we watch, what we
laugh at, what we sing, what we wear, where we go, who we cleave to, how we speak, how we handle money, how we
treat people, how we serve, and how we live when nobody is watching. A person cannot claim to be part of God’s army
while keeping an unguarded heart, careless tongue, corrupt appetite, ungodly entertainment, secret sin, or rebellious
spirit. This is why casual Christianity, as we have learned, must be rejected. God’s army cannot be built on shallow
confession, emotional excitement, and public identity without complete obedience. An exceeding great army is first a holy
army. It may be large, gifted, organised, educated, energetic, and visible, but if it is not consecrated, it cannot carry God’s
glory because the Lord is not merely looking for people who can work for Him but those who are separated unto Him.

2. Gilgal Teaches That the Reproach of Egypt Must Be Rolled Away: After Israel crossed Jordan, God brought them to
Gilgal. There, the new generation was circumcised, and the Lord said, “This day have I rolled away the reproach of Egypt
from off you.” This was a painful but necessary work. Israel had left Egypt physically, but there were covenant matters that
still had to be addressed before they could move fully into possession. Gilgal was a place of cutting, healing, renewal, and
separation. It is possible to come out of Egypt and still carry marks of Egypt. It is possible to leave an old life but still carry
old appetites. It is possible to join fellowship but still love the world. It is possible to be physically present among God’s
people while inwardly still tied to old identities. The reproach of Egypt can show up in many ways as sinful appetites,
impure thoughts, dishonest habits, pride, bitterness, prayerlessness, rebellion, worldly ambitions, careless entertainment,
corrupt friendships, secret compromise, and unbelief. These things must not be managed but must be brought to Gilgal
where the knife of God’s Word must cut what cannot enter the future with us.

Gilgal also teaches that consecration may require pain. There are things God removes that the flesh may not release easily.
There are relationships that must be redefined. There are habits that must be broken. There are conversations that must
stop. There are platforms that must be left. There are ambitions that must be surrendered. There are things on our phones
that must be deleted. There are apologies and restitutions that must be made. There are spiritual disciplines that must be
restored. Yet, the pain of cutting is better than the danger of carrying Egypt into Canaan because just as Paul says in
Ephesians, we must put off the old man and put on the new man. The Christian life is not cosmetic adjustment but a total
change of life. The old manner of life must be removed, the mind must be renewed and the new man must be expressed
in righteousness and true holiness. An exceeding great army cannot carry Egypt into the Promised Land. The reproach must
be rolled away, the old man must be put off, and the new man must be put on.

3. Hidden Sin Weakens the Army and Must Be Judged Quickly: The fall at the small city of Ai showed that hidden sin can
weaken an entire army. Israel had just seen Jericho fall by the power of God. Yet, at Ai, they were mercilessly defeated.
The problem was not military weakness but a covenant violation. God said, “Israel hath sinned.” Achan had taken the
accursed thing, hidden it among his stuff, and brought trouble upon the camp. God said they could not stand before their
enemies until the accursed thing was removed. God’s army must never treat hidden sin lightly. A secret matter can have
corporate consequences. A hidden compromise can weaken a whole family. A concealed habit can open the door to defeat.
What is buried under personal “stuff” may affect the strength of the whole camp. In contemporary life, the accursed thing
may not be a Babylonish garment or silver and gold from Jericho that Achan took. It may be secret sin, hidden dishonesty,
immoral entertainment, corrupt money, bitterness, spiritual pride, manipulation, deception, exam malpractice, false
reporting at work, ungodly relationships, secret chats, emotional attachments, or deliberate disobedience.

The danger of hidden sin is that it often grows under silence. At first, the conscience may still speak. Then, the person
begins to justify it. Then, prayer becomes weak. Then, correction becomes irritating. Then. spiritual sensitivity reduces.
This was why Week 41 warned us about backsliding: yielding to temptations, weakened resistance, self-justification,
detachment from God, seared conscience, grieving the Holy Spirit, and eventually dangerous turning away. Consecration
demands that we judge small things before they become strongholds.

God’s mercy must not be misunderstood. He is patient and gracious, but He is also holy. Joshua’s warning in Joshua 23
showed that if Israel went back and cleaved to wrong attachments, those things would become snares, traps, scourges,
and thorns. God can warn, convict, and provide a way of escape, but if His people continue to harden their hearts, the
consequences can become painful. Grace does not make sin safe. Therefore, TACEFites must practise sincere and instant
quick repentance. Do not hide what God is exposing, do not defend what the Spirit is convicting you about, do not protect

 ~ 282 ~

what is weakening your fire, confess quickly, seek help where necessary, break the wrong attachment, restore
accountability, and remove the accursed thing before it weakens the army.
.
4. Consecration Must Preserve Love, Boundaries, and Daily Watchfulness: Joshua’s later warning says, “Take good heed
therefore unto yourselves, that ye love the LORD your God.” This is one of the clearest summaries of consecration.
Consecration is not only outward separation but a guarded love. The heart must remain burning for God. The danger after
victory is that love can grow cold while activity continues. A person may still attend, serve, sing, preach, lead, or appear
committed, while inward affection for God is declining. This study has repeatedly shown that spiritual decline often begins
quietly through wrong associations, polluted entertainment, ungodly relationships, professional compromise, secret
ambition, bitterness, and prayerlessness can slowly reduce love for God. What is tolerated can later dominate. What begins
as a snare can become a trap, a scourge, and a thorn.

This is why consecration must include boundaries. Boundaries are not signs of weakness but are signs of wisdom. A believer
who loves God must guard access to the heart. Some friendships must be limited, some conversations must end, some
platforms must be avoided, and some invitations must be declined. Some films, comedy, music, and online content must
not be entertained. Some professional gatherings, reunions, and relationships must be approached with discernment. A
consecrated life does not assume that every open door is safe.

5. Step-by-Step Applications and Practical Implications
 · Return to consecration: Ask what God has been trying to remove, correct, and renew in your life.
 · Sanctify yourself before the wonders: Do not seek divine breakthroughs without spiritual preparation, obedience,
 and surrender.
 · Bring every reproach to Gilgal: Let God roll away old identities, old appetites, old relationships, old habits, and old
 shame.
 · Put off the old man: Reject former ways of speaking, thinking, reacting, relating, serving, and pursuing ambition.
 · Put on the new man: Let righteousness, true holiness, purity, truth, and love become your new lifestyle.
 · Remove the accursed thing: Do not hide sin among your personal “stuff.” Confess, repent, restore accountability,
 and obey quickly.
 · Deal with compromise early: Small tolerated sins can become strongholds if they are not judged.
 · Guard your love for God: Do not measure spirituality by attendance, service, title, or visibility. Ask whether your
 heart is still burning.
 · Set holy boundaries: Be careful with friendships, entertainment, social media, professional gatherings, private
 chats, and emotional attachments.
 · Reject casual Christianity: Do not offer worship without surrender, service without sincerity, or Christian identity
 without holiness.
 · Walk as a child of light: Let your conduct in school, workplace, home, marriage, business, ministry, and online
 spaces reflect Christ.
 · Live ready for God’s use: A consecrated life is a prepared vessel for divine assignments.

Week 51: Monday, 15 August 2027 to Sunday, 22 August 2027
Title: Summaries from Joshua, Part 2: The Art of Spiritual Warfare: Mapping, Discernment, Victory, and Pulling Down
Strongholds

Bible Texts: Joshua 5:13-15; Joshua 6:1-5; Joshua 7:10-13; Joshua 8:1-2; Joshua 9:14; Joshua 10:8, 22-25; Joshua 11:18-23;
Joshua 13:1; Ephesians 6:10-18; 2 Corinthians 10:3-5

Key Extracts from the Bible Texts to Remember and Reflect On
 · As captain of the host of the LORD am I now come.
 · Loose thy shoe from off thy foot.
 · See, I have given into thine hand Jericho.
 · The wall of the city shall fall down flat.
 · Thou canst not stand before thine enemies, until ye take away the accursed thing from among you.
 · Bring out those five kings unto me out of the cave.
 · Joshua made war a long time with all those kings.
 · Be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might.
 · Put on the whole armour of God.
 · We wrestle not against flesh and blood.
 · That ye may be able to withstand in the evil day.
 · The weapons of our warfare are not carnal.

Introduction
This week brings us to the final study in our annual journey through Joshua and Ephesians in deepening our shared
understanding on the making of an exceeding great army. In this final week, we bring the whole journey to a strategic
conclusion on how every revival army must understand the art of spiritual warfare. The book of Joshua does not merely
teach us that Israel fought battles. It shows us how God trained His people to fight. Some battles required waiting, silence,
shouting, priestly order, repentance before engagement, ambush, or exposing hidden kings. Some required long
obedience, mapping the remaining territories and sometimes some required the people to understand that the true
Commander of the battle was not Joshua, but the Captain of the host of the Lord.

This is a major lesson for TACEFites. Spiritual warfare is not random emotional excitement, fleshly confrontation, or careless
declaration. It is not fighting people or blaming everyone around us. It is not shouting at the devil while ignoring hidden
sin, poor discernment, prayerlessness, disobedience, or lack of divine strategy. Spiritual warfare is the disciplined, Spirit-
led, Word-governed, holy, discerning, and obedient engagement of God’s army against everything that resists the will,
knowledge, authority, and purpose of Christ.
Ephesians tells us clearly that we wrestle not against flesh and blood. This means the real battle behind many visible issues
is spiritual. Behind temptations, deceptions, divisions, fears, addictions, ungodly habits, family breakdowns,
prayerlessness, false doctrines, corrupt systems, and repeated patterns, there may be strongholds that must be pulled
down by weapons that are mighty through God. 2 Corinthians teaches that these strongholds include imaginations, high
things, and thoughts that exalt themselves against the knowledge of God. Therefore, spiritual warfare includes the battle
of the mind, the battle of desire, the battle of obedience, the the battle of homes, and the battle for territories. This final
week therefore commissions TACEFites into warfare intelligence because we must know the Commander. We must learn
how to map the battle, discern the strategy, understand the type of warfare before us, avoid Gibeonite deception, and
expose hidden kings. We must understand God’s way to pull down strongholds. bring thoughts, habits, homes, fellowships,
campuses, workplaces, and communities under the obedience of Christ.

Teachings
1. The Commander of the Army of the Lord - Warfare Begins with Surrender to Divine Command: Before Jericho fell,
Joshua met a man with a drawn sword. Joshua asked, “Art thou for us, or for our adversaries?” The answer was surprising:
“Nay; but as captain of the host of the LORD am I now come.” This encounter teaches one of the deepest principles of
spiritual warfare and this is whether we are surrendered to the Lord’s command. Joshua was the visible leader of Israel,
but he was not the final Commander. Before the walls of Jericho came down, Joshua had to bow to the owner of the battle.

 ~ 285 ~

Before battle came surrender. Before Joshua could command men, he had to receive command from the Lord. When he
asked, “What saith my lord unto his servant?” he moved from military confidence into servant obedience.

This is where true warfare begins. An exceeding great army must not fight from pride, anger, ambition, reaction, revenge,
offence, or human wisdom. Many people enter spiritual battles with the wrong spirit. They fight people instead of
principalities. They fight from pain instead of prayer. They fight from assumption instead of instruction. They fight to prove
themselves instead of obeying God.
.
The Captain of the Lord’s host also told Joshua to remove his shoe because the place was holy. This means the battlefield
was not ordinary ground. When God is present, warfare becomes holy service. We do not fight casually. We do not fight
with dirty hands, hidden sin, pride, or while ignoring the holiness of God. The first preparation for victory is consecrated
life.

Therefore, before fighting for territory, ask, “Lord, have I removed my shoes?” A true revival army must not rush into battle
without bowing before the Commander. We must learn to live under command of the Lord. We are not independent
soldiers. We belong to Christ and He is the Captain, the Head, the King, and the Lord of the army. Our courage, strategy,
timing, weapons, and victory must come from Him.
2. Mapping the Battle - Knowing the Territory, the Gates, the Strongholds, and the Hidden Kings: Joshua’s battles were
real. Israel faced rivers, walls, cities, kings, caves, coalitions, mountains, valleys, inheritance boundaries, and remaining
lands. A revival army had to understand what was before them. For example, Jericho was a shut city, Ai required a different
strategy, Gibeon came with deception and the five kings hid in a cave. Joshua 11 records a long war. These details teach us
that warfare requires understanding of the battlefield.

Spiritual mapping is the weapon we have in God to prayerfully discern the nature of the battle before engaging it. It is the
careful, Word-guided, Spirit-led effort to understand what is resisting the purpose of God in a life, home, fellowship,
campus, workplace, church, community, or nation. The questions we bring out in the mapping process are: What is the
pattern? What is the gate? What is the repeated failure? What is the hidden king? What stronghold is resisting the
knowledge of God? In a personal life, mapping may reveal patterns such as lust, pride, anger, fear, bitterness,
prayerlessness, unbelief, procrastination, spiritual laziness, addiction to ungodly entertainment, or repeated compromise.
In a home, mapping may reveal broken communication, inherited curses, prayerlessness, marital secrecy, financial
dishonesty, unresolved offence, ungodly media culture, or lack of discipleship for children. In a fellowship, mapping may
reveal locational stronghold, satanic influence, disunity, or dominant moral perversion.

Mapping helps us identify gates. A gate is an access point. In spiritual life, gates may include what enters through the eyes,
ears, conversations, friendships, media, sexual intimacy, relationships, money, habits, and counsel. A believer who keeps
watching corrupt content is opening a gate. A married person who keeps secret emotional conversations is opening a gate.
A professional who joins dishonest networks is opening a gate. A young person who makes mockers his closest friends is
opening a gate. A fellowship that allows gossip, offence, and disorder is opening gates to weakness. Mapping also helps
expose hidden kings. In Joshua 10, the five kings hid in a cave. They were not visible at the battlefront, but they still
represented ruling powers. In essence, as an exceeding great army, we must learn to ask spiritual questions. What is
fighting my prayer life? What keeps weakening my consecration? What pattern is repeating in my family? What keeps
limiting our local fellowship? What is discouraging our young people? What lie is shaping this community? What open gate
must be closed? What hidden king must be exposed? What territory remains unpossessed? An exceeding great army does
not fight blindly. It prays, observes, discerns, asks counsel from the Lord, studies patterns, applies the Word, and engages
the battle with understanding.

3. Warfare Types - Jericho, Ai, Gibeon, Coalitions, Long Wars, and Remaining Lands: Joshua teaches us that different
battles require different strategies. The art of spiritual warfare includes knowing the type of battle before applying the
strategy of battle. A careless army treats every battle the same way. A wise army asks God for understanding. Jericho
teaches the battle of divine timing, priestly order, obedience, and faith. The wall did not fall because Israel had the
strongest physical weapons but because the people followed God’s instruction to shout. Some battles in our lives require
obedience to instructions that may not make sense to the natural mind. God may ask us to be silent when we want to
explain. He may ask us to wait when we want to rush. He may ask us to worship when we want to panic. Jericho teaches
that obedience to divine strategy can bring down impossible walls.

 ~ 286 ~

The battle at Ai teaches the battle of hidden sin. Israel could not stand before a smaller enemy because something was
wrong in the camp. This means not every defeat is caused by external enemies. Sometimes the battle is internal. Before
shouting at the walls outside, we must ask whether there is an accursed thing inside. Some people are fighting external
battles while hiding internal compromise. Victory may not return until sin is judged, repentance is made, and obedience is
restored. The second battle of Ai teaches recovery warfare. After repentance, God told Joshua, “Fear not, neither be thou
dismayed.” Failure did not end Israel’s journey. God gave a fresh strategy and renewed courage. This teaches that when a
believer has repented sincerely, he must not remain paralysed by shame. He must rise, obey, and fight again under God’s
instruction. The engagement with Gibeon teaches the battle of deception. Israel was not defeated by swords, but by a
story. The men took of the victuals and asked not counsel at the mouth of the Lord. This is one of the greatest risks in
spiritual warfare. Not every enemy comes looking like an enemy. Some come as opportunities, partnerships, relationships,
invitations, business proposals, emotional appeals, spiritual platforms, or social connections. Discernment is therefore a
weapon because not every open door is God’s door.

4. Pulling Down Strongholds - Victory Must Move from Event to Occupation: Paul teaches that the weapons of our warfare
are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strongholds. A stronghold is anything that has become
fortified against the knowledge, will, truth, and obedience of Christ. Strongholds may exist in thoughts, desires, habits,
homes, relationships, cultures, institutions, communities, and generations. They are not pulled down by human strength,
but by weapons that are mighty through God. Strongholds are often built gradually. A thought becomes a desire; a desire
becomes a habit; a habit becomes a pattern; a pattern becomes a stronghold; and a stronghold begins to defend itself
through excuses, secrecy, pride, or self-justification. This is why Paul speaks of casting down imaginations and every high
thing that exalts itself against the knowledge of God. The battle often begins in the mind before it appears in behaviour.

In practical terms, a stronghold may be anger that controls a home, bitterness that poisons relationships, lust that weakens
purity, fear that prevents obedience, pride that rejects correction, addiction to ungodly entertainment, secret emotional
attachments, dishonest gain, unbelief, inferiority, rebellion, family curse, or repeated cycles of compromise. Pulling down
strongholds requires more than one emotional prayer. It requires truth, repentance, obedience, renewed thinking,
accountability, spiritual discipline, and replacement with godly patterns. Lies must be replaced with truth. Secrecy must be
replaced with confession and accountability. Ungodly appetite must be replaced with the Word and healthy spiritual desire.
Bitterness must be replaced with forgiveness.

In addition, Joshua’s conquest teaches that victory must move from event to occupation. It is one thing to win a battle but
it is more important to possess the land. Some believers experience moments of breakthrough but do not occupy the
territory afterwards. They pray powerfully at a retreat but return to the same habits. They repent at a meeting but do not
build new discipline. They receive conviction but do not close the gates. They defeat a king but leave the cave open.
The art of spiritual warfare therefore includes occupation or taking over the defeated space. After victory, build structures.
We must not only celebrate spiritual moments, we must possess the land. We must occupy our homes with prayer. We
must occupy our minds with truth. We must occupy our fellowships with discipleship. We must occupy our workplaces
with integrity. We must occupy our campuses with fire of revival. We must occupy our communities with gospel light. We
must occupy our generation with revival burden. An exceeding great army does not only win events; it establishes the rule
of Christ in lives, homes, territories, and generations.

5. Step-by-Step Applications and Practical Implications
 · Bow before the Commander: Do not enter warfare with pride, anger, reaction, or self-confidence. Ask, “Lord, what
 saith my Lord unto His servant?”
 · Remove your shoes: Treat warfare as holy service. Do not fight with hidden sin, pride, bitterness, or uncleanness.
 · Map the battle prayerfully: Ask what pattern, gate, lie, stronghold, hidden king, or unpossessed territory needs to
 be addressed.
 · Identify the type of warfare: Do not treat every battle the same way. Jericho, Ai, Gibeon, coalitions, and remaining
 lands require different responses.
 · Seek divine strategy: Do not assume that yesterday’s method is today’s instruction. Ask counsel from the Lord.
 · Avoid Gibeonite deception: Not every opportunity, relationship, invitation, partnership, business proposal, or
 spiritual platform is from God.
 · Close open gates: Watch what enters through your eyes, ears, friendships, chats, entertainment, habits, money,
 counsel, and relationships.

 ~ 287 ~

· Expose hidden kings: Bring fear, pride, lust, bitterness, unbelief, anger, rejection, self-rule, and secret ambition
 under the authority of Christ.
 · Pull down strongholds: Use truth, repentance, prayer, fasting, accountability, obedience, and renewed thinking.
 · Bring thoughts into obedience: Do not allow imaginations, lies, fears, and desires to rule your life against the
 knowledge of God.
 · Possess remaining lands: Past victories must not make you passive. There is still more of Christ to know, more
 souls to reach, and more territories to occupy.

TACEF Marriage Procedure: God's pattern of Christian Courtship
This guideline is provided as God-inspired instruction to guide the household of TACEF on Biblical pattern of marital choice
and post-marital procedure. We recognize the role of Heaven in giving us the best and the need to patiently seek the Lord
to get this best which comes alone from Him.

We therefore seek the understanding of the brethren to abide and align to these inspired procedures as they will help us
to collectively fulfill the will of God and mature us for Heaven in purity.

The leadership must not force their choice on others or act "god" in this eternal choice process. The leading of the Holy
Spirit must be respected at all times. Personal conviction and proven witnesses shall be considered as the most valid basis
for every conclusion reached in the process.

Marriage procedure

 • When the time comes*, brethren must pray to receive a leading to a particular brother or sister whether within or
 outside the ministry.
 *(This period is either at the final stages of education or apprenticeship and with guaranteed path of livelihood and
 emotional maturity rooted in valid Christian testimony. Marriage is not for kids).
 • Once the brother in question is convinced of the Lord, he should discuss with his Co-ordinator first. Sisters are not
 allowed to propose to brothers directly or indirectly.
 • The Co-ordinator shall notify the Marriage committee of the zone, who prays and makes necessary confirmation
 and investigations (Please note that all references to the marriage committee must be documented in black and
 white)
 • The Marriage Committee shall invite the brother for a discussion to be sure of his leading towards the particular
 sister.
 • The Marriage Committee of the zone shall nominate a member of the committee to encourage the "received" sister
 to seek the face of God concerning a life partner. No cues or prompts must be provided directly or indirectly on the
 particular brother as the discussion must remain generic and confidential.
 • If the sister comes back with a convincing leading towards the brother that had come with the proposal, the
 committee shall encourage the brother to make his proposal to the sister.
 • If the sister does not receive leading to the brother in question, the brother will not be allowed to make a proposal.
 • The sister in question is expected to inform the committee of the proposal and express her conviction, which will
 be a basis for encouraging her to give her consent.
 • If after all prayers and scrutiny, a sister is not receiving leading to the particular brother that has indicated interest
 to the committee, the brother will be invited and informed accordingly and promptly. The brother must let go
 irrespective of his "sure leading" and "many convictions".
 (However, if the brother insists, he shall be allowed to propose as a simple way to clarify the committee's position.
 This must however be discouraged)
 • After the formal proposal and acceptance, the new partners will be brought together by the Marriage committee
 for prayers and a formal commencement of Courtship. (This is after a written letter of notification to the
 committee).
 • This process is only completed when the National Marriage Committee allocates the new partner to a counselor (a
 married couple within the ministry with proven testimony of a gracious marriage). The counseling family shall use
 the national counseling study series through meetings, discussions and prayers sessions to guide the Courtship
 period; and shall provide monthly update to the National Counseling Secretary on how the couple-to-be are
 growing and coping.
 NB: If you are already in Courtship and have not been allocated a Counselor, please contact the National Executives
 using any of the contacts provided on the Contact page.
 • This process of counseling must be held at least six months before the wedding.
 • If any member relocates to another Zone and became engaged in the new zone of the ministry, the marriage
 committee of the present zone shall communicate with the marriage committee of the previous zone for
 notification and necessary clarifications, especially on the need to be sure that the member involved have no
 previous commitments and his or her Christian life can be proven.
 • All sub-zonal co-ordinators should be automatic members of the zonal marriage committee

 ~ 292 ~

• Marriage committee members shall include the Zonal/ Asst. zonal co-ordinator Sister co-ordinator, Prayer co-
 ordinator, 2 Counselors/experienced brethren, and sub-zonal co-ordinators
 • Any brethren that informs any of the marriage committee members has automatically informed the committee
 • Zonal marriage committee reports to National counseling secretary who provides activity report to the Central
 Executive Council.
 • There should be regular feedback from the marriage counselors to the zonal marriage committee

CAVEAT AND WARNINGS

1) Latest trends on use of social networking marriage (Facebook, 2go etc.) where people seek for a white/richer/older
person to marry out of selfish ambition and lust of the eyes/pride of life is NOT of God. Marriage is spiritual and it must
derive its essence ONLY from God's leading and not selfish desire to relocate, earn money or citizenship of another country.

2) Knowing the will of God in marriage is a serious matter and everyone that wants to go into Marriage must be ready to
stand by their decision, having taken time to seek the face of God genuinely. The act of changing marital decisions every
year or as a result of change of location (post-NYSC year, waiting period for a job etc.) is not of God and is often borne out
of the dictates of circumstances and we therefore need to WATCH.

3) The idea of "leading-on" where a brother or a sister creates certain forms of "impression" through exclusive use of words
(like Dearie, Dearest, Honey), undue patronage like biased visitation, emailing, sharing, caring, exchange of gift etc. When
this becomes too concentrated on a specific individual without any form of heavenly backing or a long-term commitment,
there is a growing lust and you need to watch it, lest you have led others to believe what you do not mean or intend. Sisters
are naturally emotional beings and brothers must be careful how they play with their emotions. Always mean what you say
and when you are not led by God, learn to keep silent especially brothers who love to counsel without a clear and convincing
leading from God.

4) Dating is not Biblical and it is never the way to get a partner. The emerging trend of "sampling" through multiple
relationships/friendships excludes the role of God as the ultimate one who chooses and guides every step of our marital
commitment. Be careful of this heretic message.

5) There are also those who prefer back-end arrangement, where the two individuals (brother and sister) would have met
and agreed before presenting their lying convictions to the leadership as an act of deception. This is similar to Ananias and
Sapphira and the eternal consequence of these is apparent, both in this world and in the world to come. There is an
opportunity to repent if your courtship or marriage is built on this error of commission.

FINALLY, Zonal co-ordinators/Marriage committee should be careful in the process, knowing that we are dealing with the
destiny of men. Let us be careful to avoid all forms of favouritism, partiality, bias, past knowledge of brother/sister or our
own perceived choice.

All engaged brethren shall be presented at every Convention, Easter retreat and any major programme.

TACEF Career & Business Showcase
“A City Set on a Hill” (Matthew 5:14–16)

The TACEF Career & Business Showcase is a structured platform designed to identify, validate, and promote the
professional and business capabilities within the fellowship.

It enables intentional patronage among members, strengthens trust-based relationships, and positions TACEFites as
credible kingdom professionals operating as light in their industries.
This is not just a directory but a platform for visibility, credibility, and patronage enablement system for mutual
growth and kingdom impact.

Core Vision
Many TACEFites pray for opportunities while being surrounded by answers to those prayers through many other
members who need their services or who can recommend them to others.

This initiative exists to:
 • Unlock hidden economic value within the fellowship
 • Strengthen relationships beyond spiritual gatherings
 • Build a community economy rooted in trust and excellence
 • Position members as credible kingdom professionals
 • Encourage shared prosperity within the body

Strategic Framework
The programme operates across three simple but powerful layers:
 (1) Discovery – “Who can do what?”: Structured capture of members’ skills, professions, and businesses.
 (2) Validation – “Can we trust the service: Credibility established through references, portfolios, and
 testimonials.
 (3) Visibility – “How do people find them?: Simple, consistent channels to enable discovery and patronage.

Programme Architecture
1. Central Data Collection (Google Form): A structured onboarding form capturing:
 • Personal and contact details
 • Business and service information
 • Value proposition (problem solved and differentiation)
 • Visual portfolio (images, videos, links)
 • Client references and testimonials
 • Certifications (where applicable)
 • Service availability and indicative pricing
2. Primary Distribution Channel – WhatsApp (“TACEF Marketplace”): WhatsApp will serve as the main engagement
and visibility channel like we have TACEF job sharing platform by TACEF ambassadors.

 • Weekly Showcase Drops: 1–2 featured members presented in a consistent, high-quality format
 • Category-Based Showcases (Monthly): Integrated into the monthly professional fellowship meetings as a
 "Business Spotlight Time”, when different categories of brethren are jointly showcased for awareness
 (Finance/Tax/Business set-up and Consulting; Construction and Real Estate; Food and Catering; Creative and
 Events; and Technology and Digital Services

(3) Central Directory (Digital Repository)
A simple but effective repository for access and continuity in the form of Google Sheet directory; Google Drive
portfolio folders and possible Notion page or simple website for enhanced browsing

(4) Quality and Trust Layer: Sustained credibility will be driven by:

 ~ 309 ~

• Verified service records and delivery consistency
 • Member feedback and referrals
 • Testimony culture (e.g., “I found my architect in TACEF”)
 • Peer recommendation and accountability

(5) Governance Principles: in order to maintain spiritual integrity and long-term value, the platform will be guided by
excellence over hype; integrity over profit; and service over exploitation
All participants will align with the commitment: “I commit to represent Christ through excellence, honesty, and
fairness in all services rendered.”

(6) Expected Outcomes
 • Increased intra-fellowship patronage
 • Stronger economic bonds within TACEF
 • Visibility of members as trusted professionals
 • A living testimony of kingdom collaboration and excellence
 • Building wealth and achieving financial sustainability with the great house

TACEF VISION/MANDATE

Raising an army with a vision of revival through focused discipleship, prayer and the ministry of the Word; to groom
a generation of Godly and heaven-conscious youths and adults who are conformed to the image of Christ and to live
each day to promote the purpose of God in The African Church and advance the cause of evangelism/revival to the
world at large. The fellowship is raised to be the "repairer of the breach", "to build the old waste places" and "to
raise the foundation of many generations". (Isa 58 vs 12).

It is important to know and note that:

 1. TACEF/TACESF is not an association, society or an ordinary group, it is a heavenly calling.
 2. TACEF/TACESF is not a gathering of youths, but a gathering of God's end-time army: students and non-
 students of all age groups learning under the tutelage of the Spirit of God.
 3. TACEF has a revival mandate to The African Church and will remain committed to serving God's will in the
 Church.

Our motivation is that we strongly believe that The African Church is at the threshold of a great revival in the
dispensation of God and we are fully persuaded that the Lord is equipping the Church for the end-time revival.

Our prayers and pursuit therefore shall continue to be the promotion of the purpose of God in The African Church.
We shall continue in prayers and the ministry of the word, as we trust the Lord for a season of total spiritual
awakening. We trust the Lord that in all of our local churches, the Word of God will take pre-eminence, and the Spirit
of the Lord will dominate. We believe the Lord for a rekindled passion for the dying souls under the grip of the evil
one and a renewed pursuit of holiness without which no man shall see the Lord.
